2.q: Why did the ancient Egyptians build the great pyramids?
2.e: The kings of ancient Egypt were called pharaohs. The Egyptians believed in life after death, so they built huge tombs for them: the pyramids.

3.q: Since which year has Switzerland been a modern federal state with a Federal Constitution?
3.e: 1291 is the year of the Federal Charter of the first cantons, remembered on 1 August. But the modern federal state with a shared constitution, Parliament and Federal Council has only existed since 1848.
3.m: The Federal Charter dates from 1291, the modern federal state from 1848.

4.q: In which city do the Federal Council and the Swiss Parliament sit?
4.e: Bern is the federal city of Switzerland. The Federal Palace is there, where the Federal Council works and Parliament meets.
4.m: The Federal Palace is in Bern.

37.q: Which job suits someone who really loves working with animals?
37.e: Animal keepers feed and look after animals, for example at the zoo or in an animal shelter. Many jobs fit well with what you like doing in your free time.
37.m: What you like doing can become your job.

38.q: How is an apprenticeship in Switzerland organised?
a: You work at the training company and also go to vocational school
You only work, with no school
You learn everything on your own online
38.e: The official name for an apprenticeship is basic vocational education. You learn the job at the company, go to vocational school one or two days a week, and also attend inter-company courses.
38.m: In an apprenticeship you learn at the company and at school.

a: A few days at a company to get to know a job
The final exam of the apprenticeship
39.e: On a taster placement you work alongside others at a company for a few days. You find out whether you like the job, and the company gets to know you. It is often the first step towards an apprenticeship.
39.m: On a taster placement you try out a job.

40.q: What does the abbreviation EFZ stand for?
40.e: You receive the EFZ after a three- or four-year apprenticeship. It shows that you have learned a trade and is recognised throughout Switzerland.
40.m: The EFZ is the qualification from a 3- to 4-year apprenticeship.

59.q: Where can you keep money safely?
59.e: In a bank account your money is protected from theft and fire. You can always see how much you have and withdraw it when you need it.
59.m: A bank account is a safe place for money.

60.q: What is interest on a savings account?
a: Money the bank pays you for keeping your money there
60.e: The bank works with your money, for example by lending it out. In return it pays you a small amount: the interest. How much depends on the bank and the period of time.
60.m: Interest is a reward for saving.

61.q: What is the difference between a debit card and a credit card?
a: A debit card takes money straight from your account, a credit card bills you later
A debit card gives you credit
A credit card is only for children
61.e: With a debit card the amount is taken from your account straight away, so you only spend what is there. With a credit card you get a bill at the end of the month. That is handy, but it is easier to lose track.
61.m: With a debit card you pay now, with a credit card later.

63.q: What does a Swiss IBAN start with?
63.e: The IBAN is your international account number. Swiss IBANs start with the country code CH. Other people can use it to send you money.
63.m: A Swiss IBAN starts with CH.

76.q: Which number do you call for the fire brigade in Switzerland?
76.e: Switzerland has three important emergency numbers: 117 for the police, 118 for the fire brigade and 144 for the ambulance. 112 also works everywhere in Europe.
76.m: The police number is 117, the fire brigade 118 and the ambulance 144.

77.q: What do you do when the pedestrian light is red?
a: Go if no car is coming
77.e: Red means stop. You may only go when it is green, and even then look left and right quickly to check that all the cars really stop.
77.m: At red you stop, at green you look and then go.

a: A long sentence with numbers and symbols that only you know
78.e: Long passwords are hard to guess. A whole sentence like “My dog eats 3 carrots!” is easy to remember and hard to crack. Never use the same password everywhere.
78.m: A safe password is long, unique and secret.

80.q: What is the name of the hero who, according to legend, shot an apple off his son's head?
80.e: William Tell is the best-known legendary figure in Switzerland. According to the legend, he had to shoot an apple off his son's head on the orders of the bailiff Gessler. Whether Tell really lived has not been proven.
80.m: Tell is the legendary hero with the crossbow.

84.q: Which empire built towns such as Aventicum (Avenches) in what is now Switzerland?
84.e: About 2000 years ago, the area of present-day Switzerland belonged to the Roman Empire. Aventicum was an important town with a theatre and a town wall, and you can still see remains of it today.

92.q: Who started the founding of the Red Cross?
92.e: In 1859, Henry Dunant witnessed the Battle of Solferino and saw the suffering of the wounded. His book about it led to the founding of the Red Cross in Geneva in 1863. In 1901 he received the first Nobel Peace Prize.
92.m: Henri Dunant started the founding of the Red Cross in Geneva.

167.q: What do people in Switzerland call the machine where you can withdraw cash?
167.e: In Switzerland people usually say Bancomat. With a card and your PIN you can withdraw cash from your account there.
167.m: You can withdraw cash at a Bancomat.

168.q: What do you do with the PIN for your card?
a: Keep it secret and tell nobody
168.e: The PIN is a secret number. Anyone who knows it and has the card can withdraw your money. Cover the keypad when you type it in.

169.e: The Swiss National Bank (SNB) is Switzerland's central bank. It issues the banknotes and makes sure the franc stays stable. It has offices in Bern and Zurich.

a: A Swiss app for paying with your phone
170.e: With TWINT you can pay with your smartphone or send money to friends. The app is linked to your bank account or a prepaid balance.
170.m: With TWINT you can pay with your phone.

a: A regular automatic payment, for example for the rent
An order that is never carried out
171.e: With a standing order the bank automatically transfers the same amount every month. Handy for rent or a phone contract, so you never forget a payment.
171.m: A standing order pays an amount automatically every month.

172.q: What replaced the old orange payment slip in Switzerland?
172.e: Since autumn 2022 there has only been the QR-bill. You scan the QR code with your banking app and all the payment details are filled in automatically.
172.m: You can simply scan and pay a QR-bill.

173.q: What does a bank statement show?
a: All the money coming into and going out of your account
173.e: On the bank statement or in the app you can see when money came in or went out. If you check it regularly, you will also spot wrong payments.
173.m: A bank statement gives an overview of your account.

214.q: Who repairs cars at the garage?
214.e: At the garage, car mechanics check and repair engines and brakes. Today the job is called automotive mechatronics technician.

215.e: Hairdressers advise customers and cut and colour hair. Creativity and enjoying contact with people are important here.

216.q: Which path do most young people in Switzerland choose after compulsory school?
216.e: About two thirds of young people in Switzerland do an apprenticeship. The dual system with company and school is seen as a model internationally.
216.m: An apprenticeship is the most common path.

a: A written contract between apprentice and company, approved by the canton
217.e: The apprenticeship contract sets out the length, wages, holidays and working hours. For under-18s, the parents sign too. The cantonal vocational training office must approve the contract.
217.m: An apprenticeship contract is written and approved by the canton.

a: Courses outside the training company where basic skills are practised
218.e: In the üK, all apprentices in a trade learn the most important basics, no matter which company they work for. That way everyone has the same foundation.
218.m: In inter-company courses (üK) you learn shared basics.

219.q: What belongs in an application for an apprenticeship?
a: A cover letter, CV and school reports
219.e: In the cover letter you explain why the job interests you. Add your CV, school reports and often taster placement reports or test results.
219.m: An application includes a letter, CV and reports.

224.q: What should you wear when you ride a bike?
224.e: A helmet protects your head if you fall. It is important that it fits well and the strap is fastened.
224.m: When you ride a bike, you put on a helmet.

225.q: Which side of the road do people drive on in Switzerland?
225.e: Switzerland drives on the right: bikes and cars use the right-hand side. In Great Britain, on the other hand, people drive on the left.
225.m: In Switzerland people drive on the right.

226.q: Where does an empty PET bottle go?
226.e: You can return PET bottles to many shops. New bottles are made from the material. That saves raw materials and energy.
226.m: Empty PET bottles go back to the collection.

227.q: Why do you wash your hands before eating?
a: To make the food taste better
227.e: Bacteria and viruses collect on your hands. Washing with soap and water for about 20 seconds removes most of them. That way you get ill less often.
227.m: Washing your hands means fewer germs.

228.q: Which number do you call in Switzerland in case of poisoning?
228.e: Tox Info Suisse gives advice on 145 day and night in cases of poisoning, for example if a child has swallowed cleaning products or tablets. If someone is unconscious, call 144 straight away.

229.q: Which number do you call to alert Rega, the Swiss air rescue service?
229.e: Rega flies injured people to hospital in helicopters and air ambulance jets, for example after an accident in the mountains. You can reach it on 1414.

230.q: According to the food pyramid, what should you eat or drink the most of?
230.e: The base is unsweetened drinks like water, then come vegetables and fruit, then cereals. Sweet and salty foods are at the top, so only a little of those.
230.m: Drink plenty of water, eat lots of vegetables and fruit and few sweet things.

231.q: Why do many municipalities charge a fee for rubbish bags?
a: Whoever makes more rubbish should pay more
So that rubbish costs more than food
231.e: The bag fee follows the polluter pays principle: whoever produces lots of rubbish pays more. That encourages people to collect glass, paper and PET separately.
231.m: Whoever makes rubbish pays for it: the bag fee follows the polluter pays principle.

249.q: What were the kings of ancient Egypt called?
249.e: The pharaohs ruled ancient Egypt and were worshipped like gods. One of the best known is Tutankhamun, whose tomb full of treasure was discovered in 1922.
249.m: The kings of ancient Egypt were called pharaohs.

250.q: Where do the Olympic Games originally come from?
250.e: The first Olympic Games took place about 2800 years ago in Olympia in Greece, in honour of the god Zeus. The modern Games have existed since 1896.

251.q: What is the picture writing of the ancient Egyptians called?
251.e: Hieroglyphs are made up of small pictures for sounds and words. For a long time nobody could read them. Only with the Rosetta Stone were they deciphered in the 19th century.
251.m: The writing of the ancient Egyptians is called hieroglyphs.

252.q: What did the Romans build to carry water into their towns?
252.e: Aqueducts were water channels with a gentle slope, often running over high arched bridges. This way fresh water flowed for many kilometres to fountains and baths.
252.m: The Romans built aqueducts to carry water into their towns.

253.q: In which ancient city did an early form of democracy develop?
253.e: In ancient Athens, free men could take part in decisions in the people's assembly. Women, slaves and foreigners, however, were excluded. The word democracy means ‘rule by the people’.

254.q: Which volcano buried the Roman town of Pompeii in the year 79?
254.e: When Vesuvius erupted, Pompeii was buried under ash. This preserved the town, and today you can visit its streets, houses and wall paintings.

255.e: Caesar conquered Gaul and became the most powerful man in Rome. Because many feared he wanted to become king, he was murdered on the Ides of March in 44 BC.
255.m: Julius Caesar was a Roman general and was murdered in 44 BC.

258.q: What do Socrates, Plato and Aristotle have in common?
a: They were famous philosophers in ancient Greece
258.e: The three thinkers lived in Greece about 2400 years ago. They asked questions such as what justice is and how to live a good life. Their ideas still shape our thinking today.
258.m: Socrates, Plato and Aristotle were Greek philosophers.

276.q: Which three places are seen as the founders of the Swiss Confederation?
276.e: According to tradition, the three “original cantons” joined together in 1291 to help each other. Unterwalden is now divided into Obwalden and Nidwalden.
276.m: The original cantons are Uri, Schwyz and Unterwalden.

277.q: On which lake is the Rütli meadow?
277.e: The Rütli is on Lake Lucerne. According to legend, men from the original cantons swore eternal loyalty to each other there. Celebrations take place there on 1 August.
277.m: The Rütli is the symbolic place of the Swiss Confederation.

278.q: Which battle did the Confederates win against a Habsburg army in 1315?
278.e: At Morgarten, men from Schwyz surprised a Habsburg army of knights on a narrow path between the mountain and the lake. The victory strengthened the alliance of the Confederates.
278.m: In 1315, the Confederates won at Morgarten.

279.q: What happened to the Old Swiss Confederacy in 1798?
a: French troops marched in, and the Helvetic Republic was created
The Habsburgs conquered the whole country
The cantons founded the federal state
279.e: In 1798, revolutionary France occupied Switzerland. The old order with subject territories was abolished and a unified state, the Helvetic Republic, was founded. It lasted only a few years.
279.m: The Helvetic Republic was created in 1798.

280.q: When was Switzerland's neutrality recognised by the great powers of Europe?
a: In 1815 at the Congress of Vienna
280.e: After the end of the Napoleonic Wars, in 1815 the great powers recognised Switzerland's permanent neutrality. Today's borders also largely date from this time.

285.q: In which year was the Gotthard Base Tunnel, the longest railway tunnel in the world, opened?
285.e: The Gotthard Base Tunnel is about 57 kilometres long and was opened in 2016. Since then, goods and people can travel through the Alps faster and on a flatter route. The first Gotthard railway tunnel dates from 1882.
285.m: The 57 km Gotthard Base Tunnel was opened in 2016.

386.q: What is a savings account for?
a: To put money aside for longer
386.e: In a savings account you put aside money you don't need straight away. There is often a little more interest than on an everyday account.
386.m: In a savings account you put money aside.

a: Sending money from one account to another
387.e: With a transfer you tell the bank to send money to another account, for example to pay a bill. You need the IBAN of the person receiving it.
387.m: With a transfer, money goes from one account to another.

388.q: What do many banks offer especially for young people?
388.e: Many banks have accounts for children and young people, often without account fees and with their own card. That way you learn early how to handle money. For under-18s, the parents usually have to agree.
388.m: A youth account is a cheap way to start.

398.q: Who makes bread and croissants in the bakehouse?
398.e: Bakers and confectioners often start very early in the morning so that the bread is fresh. The apprenticeship lasts three years and ends with the EFZ.
398.m: The bakery makes bread and croissants.

399.q: What can you do at a careers fair?
a: Get to know lots of jobs and talk to apprentices and companies
399.e: At careers fairs, many jobs and companies present themselves. You can try out tasks and ask apprentices directly what their everyday working life is like.
399.m: At a careers fair you can discover jobs.

400.q: What is true about apprentices' wages?
a: They are set in the apprenticeship contract and usually rise each year
They are always as high as for fully trained workers
400.e: Apprentices receive a wage that is written in the apprenticeship contract. It is lower than for trained workers, because you are still learning, and usually rises from year to year. There are big differences between jobs.
400.m: An apprentice's wage rises each year of training.

402.q: What is the rule at a zebra crossing in Switzerland?
a: Pedestrians have right of way, but always look first
Cars always have right of way
You must not cross the road there
402.e: Anyone clearly wanting to cross at a zebra crossing has right of way. Even so: wait until the cars stop and make eye contact with the drivers.
402.m: At a zebra crossing you have right of way, but look first.

403.q: Which emergency number works all over Europe, including Switzerland?
403.e: 112 is the European emergency number. In Switzerland it puts you through to the police. The ambulance (144) and fire brigade (118) have their own numbers.
403.m: 112 is the emergency number all over Europe.

a: Edible food that is thrown away
404.e: A large share of food ends up in the bin even though it could still be eaten. Tips against it: shop carefully, use up leftovers and, at the best-before date, smell and taste rather than throwing food away at once.
404.m: You avoid food waste by planning and using up leftovers.

406.q: What does the abbreviation CH stand for?
406.e: CH is the abbreviation of the Latin name of Switzerland: Confoederatio Helvetica, the Swiss Confederation. Latin is neutral and is not one of the four national languages.

407.q: Since when has the franc been the shared currency of Switzerland?
407.e: Before 1850, there were lots of different coins from the cantons and towns in Switzerland. With the new federal state, the franc was introduced as a single currency.

408.q: Who gave Switzerland a new order with the Act of Mediation in 1803?
408.e: The Helvetic Republic was divided by quarrels. In 1803, Napoleon arranged a new constitution, the Act of Mediation. New cantons were created, such as Aargau, Thurgau, St Gallen, the Grisons, Ticino and Vaud.
408.m: In 1803, Napoleon gave Switzerland the Act of Mediation.

409.q: Which route did the first railway running entirely in Switzerland travel in 1847?
409.e: In 1847, the first railway inside Switzerland connected Zurich with Baden. It is called the “Spanish Bun Railway” because it supposedly brought a popular pastry from Baden quickly to Zurich.
409.m: In 1847, the Spanish Bun Railway ran from Zurich to Baden.

419.q: Who was the highest god of the ancient Greeks?
419.e: The Greeks believed in many gods who lived on Mount Olympus. Zeus was their king and, according to legend, hurled thunderbolts. Thor and Odin are Norse gods.
419.m: The father of the Greek gods was Zeus.

420.q: With which special war animals did the general Hannibal cross the Alps?
420.e: More than 2000 years ago, Hannibal of Carthage crossed the Alps with an army and war elephants to attack Rome. Many of the animals did not survive the cold.
420.m: Hannibal crossed the Alps with elephants.

421.q: What is the famous amphitheatre in Rome where gladiators fought called?
421.e: The Colosseum had room for tens of thousands of spectators. Gladiator fights and animal hunts took place there. Today it is one of the best-known buildings in the world.

422.q: Which of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World is still standing today?
422.e: Of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World, only the Pyramids of Giza have survived. The others were destroyed by earthquakes, fire or decay.
422.m: The pyramids are the only surviving wonder of the ancient world.

423.q: Which language did the ancient Romans speak?
423.e: The Romans spoke Latin. Italian, French, Spanish and Romansh developed from it. Many German and English words also come from Latin, for example the German ‘Fenster’ (window) and ‘Mauer’ (wall).

a: The last queen of ancient Egypt
A pharaoh who built the pyramids
424.e: Cleopatra ruled in the 1st century BC. She allied herself with Caesar and later with Mark Antony. After her death in 30 BC, Egypt became a Roman province.
424.m: Cleopatra was the last queen of Egypt.

425.q: What is Alexander the Great known for?
a: He conquered a huge empire from Greece to India
He built the Great Wall of China
425.e: Alexander became king of Macedonia at 20. In only about ten years he conquered the Persian Empire and marched as far as India. He died aged just 32.
425.m: Alexander the Great conquered an empire reaching as far as India.

426.q: Which huge border fortification was built in China from ancient times onwards?
426.e: The first sections of wall were built more than 2000 years ago. Over many centuries they were extended and strengthened. Most of the parts you can see today date from the later Ming period.
426.m: The Great Wall of China was built over centuries.

645.q: Which emergency number belongs to this vehicle?
645.e: This is a fire engine. In Switzerland you can reach the fire brigade on 118.
645.m: You can reach the fire brigade on 118.

646.q: What does this symbol stand for?
646.e: The three arrows in a circle stand for recycling. New products are made from collected glass, paper or PET.

654.q: What is the Swiss app called that lets you pay with your phone?
654.e: With TWINT you pay in shops or send money to friends, straight from your phone.
654.m: With TWINT you can pay with your phone.

656.q: Which ancient civilisation do these pictures make you think of?
656.e: Pyramids, camels and desert sun go with ancient Egypt on the Nile.

660.q: Which legendary figure goes with these pictures?
660.e: William Tell is said to have shot an apple off his son's head with a crossbow.
660.m: An apple and a crossbow belong to William Tell.

661.q: Which Swiss holiday is celebrated with bonfires on the hills and fireworks?
661.e: On the national holiday, 1 August, there are bonfires on the hills, paper lanterns and fireworks.
661.m: On 1 August, Switzerland celebrates its National Day.

671.e: Bread and croissants are baked at the bakery.

673.q: Which country does this flag belong to?
673.e: This is the flag of Switzerland: a white cross on a red background. The Swiss flag is square.
673.m: The Swiss flag shows a white cross on red.

770.q: Which symbol is in the centre of the Israeli flag?
770.e: The blue Star of David between two blue stripes is the central symbol of the Israeli flag, introduced in 1948. It is a traditional symbol of Judaism.
770.m: Israel's flag shows the Star of David.

1054.q: Which animal is part of the coat of arms of the Principality of Liechtenstein?
1054.e: Liechtenstein's coat of arms is divided into several fields. One of them shows a black eagle on a gold background. Above it sits the princely crown.
1054.m: Liechtenstein's coat of arms includes an eagle.

1209.q: What is the leopard's spotted coat mainly for?
1209.e: The spots break up the shape of the body in light and shadow. So the leopard is hard to spot in tall grass and among branches.

1235.q: How endangered is the Amur leopard?
1235.e: There are only very few Amur leopards left in the wild. It is considered critically endangered.
1235.m: The Amur leopard is extremely rare.

1239.q: What body shape does the brown trout have?
1239.e: Its torpedo-like shape lets it glide easily through the water. So it can swim well even in strong currents.

1245.q: The trout's lateral line is marked in the picture. What is it for?
a: It senses movements in the water
1245.e: The lateral line organ senses the tiniest currents and changes in pressure. So the trout notices prey and enemies, even in murky water.
1245.m: The lateral line senses water movements.

1258.q: Which animal has been a symbol of wisdom since ancient times and often appears on university coats of arms?
1258.e: In ancient Greece the owl was the companion animal of Athena, the goddess of wisdom. That is why it still stands for cleverness and knowledge today.

1287.q: What are the ears of the African wild dog like?
1287.e: The big, round ears catch your eye straight away. They help the animal hear sounds well.
1287.m: Big round ears are a way to recognise it.

1366.q: Which animals can be seen on the coat of arms of the canton of Thurgau?
1366.e: The coat of arms of the canton of Thurgau is divided diagonally into white and green and shows two golden lions standing upright. It goes back to the Counts of Kyburg.
1366.m: Thurgau has two lions on its coat of arms.

1453.q: Which large bird of prey was wiped out in the Swiss Alps and has been successfully reintroduced since the 1990s?
1453.e: People wrongly believed the bearded vulture to be dangerous and therefore wiped it out. Since 1991 it has been deliberately released back into the Alps.
1453.m: The bearded vulture is returning to the Alps.

1457.q: How does a leopard mark its territory?
a: With scent marks and scratch marks
1457.e: Leopards use urine and scents and scratch trees. That way other leopards know the area is taken.
1457.m: Leopards mark with scent and scratch marks.

1476.q: Where does the lake trout, a relative of the brown trout, live?
a: In large lakes, swimming up inflowing rivers to spawn
1476.e: The lake trout grows up in large, deep lakes. To spawn, it swims into streams and rivers.
1476.m: Lake trout spawn in rivers flowing into the lake.

1478.q: Why are wild dogs sometimes hunted by farmers?
a: Because people fear they kill livestock
1478.e: Some people fear for their livestock and therefore hunt wild dogs. This is one reason why their numbers are falling.
1478.m: Conflicts with people threaten wild dogs.

1555.q: A trout's skin feels slippery. What is the layer of slime for?
a: It stores food for the winter
1555.e: The slime protects the skin from germs and makes the fish smooth. That is why you should always hold fish with wet hands.
1555.m: The slime protects the fish's skin.

1586.q: What does the leopard need its long tail for?
1586.e: The long tail helps the leopard keep its balance, especially on branches. It is about two thirds as long as the body.

1693.q: How big is a pack of African wild dogs usually?
1693.e: A pack usually has about 6 to 20 animals. Sometimes there are more.
1693.m: A pack usually has 6 to 20 animals.

1781.q: What is different about wild dog packs compared with many other animals?
a: The females often leave the pack
1781.e: In wild dogs it is usually the females that leave and look for a new pack. The males more often stay in the pack they were born in.
1781.m: Wild dog females often move away.

1782.q: Which animal has a long trunk and huge ears?
1782.e: The elephant is the largest land animal and uses its trunk to grab, drink and smell. Elephants live in Africa and Asia.

1851.q: How long does an adult brown trout usually grow?
1851.e: Most brown trout grow 20 to 40 centimetres long. In very good waters, some can grow much bigger.
1851.m: It usually grows 20 to 40 cm long.

1969.q: Which mammal, a good swimmer and diver, also hunts brown trout?
1969.e: The otter mainly eats fish. Beavers, muskrats and coypus also swim well, but they eat plants.

1992.q: Anglers release young trout from a fish farm into streams. Why do they do this?
a: So that there are more fish in the stream again
So that the stream gets cleaner
So that the trout eat less
So that the fish farm becomes empty
1992.e: When there are too few fish in a stream, young fish from a farm are released. Experts call this stocking. It is better if the fish can breed in the stream on their own.
1992.m: Releasing young fish is called stocking.

2011.q: Where does the word “leopard” originally come from?
2011.e: People used to believe the leopard was a mix of a lion and a pard. That is where the word comes from, from the Greek parts “leon” and “pardos”.

2095.q: Which of these animals is the African wild dog most closely related to?
2095.e: Like the wolf, the African wild dog belongs to the dog family. Despite its spots, it is not closely related to hyenas.
2095.m: The wild dog is related to the wolf, not the hyena.

2148.q: Roughly how long do young leopards stay with their mother?
a: They leave her after a week
2148.e: The young learn to hunt from their mother. At about 18 to 24 months they become independent.
2148.m: Young leopards learn for two years.

2251.q: Which statement about the African wild dog is true?
a: It is a hunter that lives in groups
2251.e: It lives and hunts in a close-knit group. That makes it a very social predator.
2251.m: Wild dogs are very social animals.

2261.q: Many African wild dogs live in the Selous Game Reserve. Which continent is it on?
2261.e: The Selous Game Reserve (now Nyerere National Park) is in the south of Tanzania in Africa. It is one of the most important areas for African wild dogs.
2261.m: The Selous Game Reserve is in Tanzania in Africa.

2272.q: Which large predator with white fur lives on the Arctic ice?
2272.e: The polar bear is the largest predator on land and lives in the Arctic, not at the South Pole. Its thick fur and a layer of fat protect it from the cold.
2272.m: The polar bear lives on the Arctic ice.

2350.q: What does the brown trout use to take in oxygen from the water?
2350.e: Water flows through the mouth and over the gills. There the oxygen passes into the blood.

2381.q: Which animal has been the most common symbol of courage and kingship in European heraldry since the Middle Ages?
2381.e: The lion has been the most common heraldic animal in Europe since the Middle Ages and stands for courage, strength and kingship. It appears on the coats of arms of England, Belgium and the Netherlands, among others.
2381.m: The lion symbolises courage and kingship.

2447.q: What is the study of coats of arms, featuring animals such as lions, eagles and leopards, called?
2447.e: Heraldry deals with coats of arms. They often show animals, for example the bear on the coat of arms of Bern or the ibex on the coat of arms of the Grisons.
2447.m: Heraldry is the study of coats of arms.

2568.q: How does a leopard usually kill its prey?
a: With a powerful bite to the throat or neck
2568.e: The leopard grabs its prey with its powerful canine teeth. It often kills smaller animals with a bite to the neck.
2568.m: Leopards kill with a powerful bite.

2583.q: Which danger particularly threatens the African wild dog?
a: Too many fish in the water
2583.e: People are using more and more land for fields and settlements. This makes the wild dogs' habitat smaller.

2611.q: Which group of fish does the brown trout belong to?
2611.e: Predatory fish eat other animals. The brown trout hunts insect larvae, crayfish and small fish.
2611.m: The brown trout is a predatory fish.

2623.q: Which animal is the largest land mammal still living in the wild in Europe?
2623.e: The European bison, also called the wisent, was almost extinct and was saved by special breeding programmes. Today it lives in selected protected areas.
2623.m: The European bison is Europe's largest land mammal.

2631.q: What shape are a leopard's pupils?
2631.e: Big cats like the leopard have round pupils. Small cats like the house cat often have slit-shaped pupils.

2634.q: What do researchers look at to tell individual wild dogs apart?
2634.e: Because each animal has its own pattern of patches, individual wild dogs can be recognised in photos. This lets researchers observe packs.
2634.m: The coat pattern gives away each individual animal.

2782.q: How endangered is the African wild dog according to the IUCN Red List?
a: It is only known in zoos
2782.e: The IUCN classes it as “endangered”. There are only a few thousand animals left.
2782.m: The African wild dog is endangered.

2841.q: In which habitats can a leopard be found?
2841.e: Leopards are very adaptable. They live in savannahs, forests, mountains and sometimes even close to cities.

2953.q: The scientific name of the African wild dog means roughly “painted wolf”. Why does that fit?
2953.e: The wild dog's coat has patches of black, yellow, brown and white. It looks as if someone has painted the animal.

3060.q: What colour is the fur of a typical leopard?
3060.e: A typical leopard has yellowish to golden brown fur with dark rosettes. The belly is lighter.
3060.m: Leopard fur is golden brown with rosettes.

3177.q: Which statement about the leopard compared with the lion and the tiger is true?
a: It is smaller than the lion and the tiger
It is bigger than the tiger
It is the biggest cat in the world
It is the same size as a lynx
3177.e: The leopard is a medium-sized big cat. Lions and tigers are much heavier.
3177.m: The leopard is smaller than the lion and the tiger.

3222.q: How many cubs does a female leopard usually have per litter?
3222.e: A female leopard usually has two to three cubs, rarely only one. The cubs are born blind.
3222.m: Leopards usually have two to three cubs.

3250.q: Which animal miaows and is one of the most popular pets in Switzerland?
3250.e: The cat is the most common pet in Switzerland. Many cats go outdoors and hunt little mice.
3250.m: The cat is a popular Swiss pet.

3260.q: Which animal has a very long neck so it can eat the highest leaves?
3260.e: The giraffe is the tallest land animal in the world and has a neck up to two metres long. This lets it reach leaves high up in the treetops.
3260.m: The giraffe has the longest neck.

3279.q: Which big cat is the fastest over short distances?
3279.e: The cheetah is the fastest land animal in the world and briefly reaches over 100 km/h. Leopards, lions and tigers are much slower.
3279.m: The cheetah is the fastest land animal.

3470.q: Which animal hops on strong back legs and carries its young in a pouch?
3470.e: The kangaroo lives in Australia and can jump very far with its strong legs. The young grow up in their mother's pouch.
3470.m: The kangaroo carries its babies in a pouch.

3490.q: Which country calls itself the “Land of the Thunder Dragon” and still shows the dragon on its flag today?
3490.e: Bhutan is also called the “Land of the Thunder Dragon”. The yellow and orange halves of the flag stand for worldly and spiritual power.
3490.m: Bhutan's flag shows a thunder dragon.

3625.q: How does a leopard typically hunt?
a: It sneaks up and makes a short dash
It chases its prey for hours
3625.e: The leopard creeps as close as possible to its prey. Then it overpowers it with a short sprint.
3625.m: Leopards sneak up on their prey.

3634.q: Which animal is often called the “king of the animals” and lives in Africa?
3634.e: Because of its strength and courage, the lion is seen as the king of the animals. Lions live in groups called prides.
3634.m: The lion is seen as the king of the animals.

3653.q: Which animal is the biggest animal in the world and lives in the sea?
3653.e: The blue whale is the biggest animal that has ever lived on Earth. It can grow over 30 metres long.
3653.m: The blue whale is the biggest animal of all.

3657.q: What does it show when a wild dog opens its mouth slightly and approaches others in a friendly way?
a: It is showing affection to the pack
It wants to run away at once
3657.e: Wild dogs often greet each other with sounds and body contact. This strengthens the bond within the pack.
3657.m: Greetings strengthen the bond in the pack.

3728.q: Roughly how fast can an African wild dog run when hunting?
a: Up to about 60 kilometres per hour
3728.e: Over a short distance it reaches about 60 kilometres per hour. That is much faster than an everyday bike ride.

3792.q: What colour is the tip of the tail of many African wild dogs?
3792.e: The white tail tip works like a signal. It helps the animals keep each other in sight when hunting in tall grass.
3792.m: The white tail tip helps them find their way.

3808.q: In which country is Kruger National Park, where wild dogs live?
3808.e: Wild dogs live in Kruger National Park in South Africa. It is one of the best-known protected areas in Africa.
3808.m: Wild dogs live in Kruger National Park.

3840.q: Which animal is known for being slow and carries its shell on its back like a house?
3840.e: The tortoise always carries its hard shell with it like a house. When in danger, it can hide its head and legs completely inside.
3840.m: The tortoise carries its house with it.

3892.q: Which disease, which can also affect pet dogs, is dangerous for wild dogs?
3892.e: Diseases such as rabies and distemper can be passed from pet dogs to wild dogs. This can threaten whole packs.
3892.m: Pet dogs can pass diseases on to wild dogs.

3927.q: Which animal can be seen on the coat of arms of the canton of Appenzell Innerrhoden?
3927.e: The coat of arms of Appenzell Innerrhoden shows a black bear on a white background. The bear comes from the Abbey of St Gallen, which Appenzell used to belong to.
3927.m: Appenzell Innerrhoden has a bear on its coat of arms.

3942.q: Which way does a brown trout usually face in a stream?
a: With its head against the current
With its head in the direction of the current
3942.e: This way fresh water reaches its gills and food drifts straight towards it. With a few flicks of its fins it stays in place.

3947.q: The picture shows a newly hatched trout with a sac on its belly. What is it for?
a: It is a yolk sac and provides food
3947.e: The yolk sac contains nutrients. The little fish lives on it for the first few weeks.
3947.m: The yolk sac feeds the young fish.

4018.q: On which continents do wild leopards live?
4018.e: Leopards live in Africa and parts of Asia. There are no wild leopards in America or Australia.
4018.m: Leopards live in Africa and Asia.

4031.q: Roughly how long does an African wild dog live in the wild?
4031.e: In the wild they usually live to around 10 to 12 years. But many die earlier from disease or other dangers.
4031.m: Wild dogs live to about ten years.

4058.q: How do injured or sick wild dogs often get treated in the pack?
a: They are driven away at once
4058.e: Pack members also share food with sick or old animals. This shows how strong the bond is.
4058.m: Wild dogs look after each other.

4099.q: Roughly how long is a female leopard pregnant?
4099.e: Pregnancy lasts around 90 to 105 days. That is about three months.
4099.m: Leopards are pregnant for about three months.

4110.q: What helps to protect the African wild dog?
4110.e: Protected areas preserve habitat, and vaccinations protect against disease. Working with local people also helps.

4150.q: What does a trout use its swim bladder for?
a: It helps it float at one depth in the water
4150.e: The swim bladder is filled with gas and provides buoyancy. That way the fish can float without much effort.

4155.q: Where do African wild dogs usually give birth to their pups?
a: In a nest made of feathers
4155.e: They often use abandoned burrows of other animals. The pups are safe there.
4155.m: Pups grow up in an underground den.

4181.q: Which organisation uses a light blue flag with a map of the world surrounded by a white olive wreath?
4181.e: The UN flag shows a map of the world framed by two olive branches as a symbol of peace. The UN was founded in 1945 and the flag introduced in 1947.
4181.m: The UN flag stands for peace worldwide.

a: A leopard or jaguar with black fur
4298.e: Black panthers are usually leopards or jaguars whose bodies make especially large amounts of dark pigment. In slanting light you can often still see the spots.
4298.m: A black panther is usually a black leopard or jaguar.

4339.q: In which landscape does the African wild dog live most often?
a: In the high mountains of the Alps
4339.e: It needs open country where it can hunt its prey well. It usually avoids dense rainforests and deserts.
4339.m: Wild dogs need open country for hunting.

4366.e: Forests are cleared, and leopards are hunted for their fur. There are also conflicts with people when livestock is killed.
4366.m: Habitat loss and poaching threaten leopards.

4371.q: Who usually has the pups in a pack?
a: All the females at the same time
4371.e: Usually only the highest-ranking pair breeds. The other animals help raise the young.
4371.m: Usually only the leading pair has pups.

4379.q: In the picture a trout is jumping. What does it often do this for?
a: To get over small obstacles and steps
To hunt birds in the air
4379.e: Brown trout can jump over small waterfalls and weirs. Sometimes they also leap for insects.

4388.q: Which animal with big round ears and a colourful coat of yellow, black and white patches can you see in the picture?
4388.e: The African wild dog has an irregular, patchy coat. Each animal has its own pattern, a bit like a fingerprint.
4388.m: Every wild dog has a unique coat pattern.

4456.q: What are the ring-shaped spots in a leopard's fur called?
4456.e: The leopard's spots are arranged in rings and look like little roses. That is why they are called rosettes.
4456.m: Leopards have rosettes in their fur.

4474.q: Which animal lives in the Swiss Alps, is a good climber and is often confused with the chamois?
4474.e: The ibex and the chamois look alike, but the ibex is much bigger and has much thicker, ridged horns. Both species live above the tree line.
4474.m: The ibex and the chamois are often confused.

4480.q: How are wild leopards doing in the world today?
a: There are many more every year
4480.e: Leopards are considered threatened worldwide. They are losing habitat and are poached. Some subspecies are already very rare.

4489.q: You see a picture of a leopard with jet-black fur. What is it often called?
4489.e: A leopard with black fur is often called a black panther. In good light you can still faintly see its rosettes.
4489.m: The black panther is a leopard.

4500.q: What does it mean that leopards are mostly solitary?
a: They mostly live and hunt alone
They only live alone in zoos
4500.e: Adult leopards usually live alone and defend a territory. Only mothers with young go around together.

4514.q: Which animal has long, curved horns and climbs steep rocks in the Alps?
4514.e: The ibex lives high in the mountains and can climb steep rock faces thanks to its special hooves. The chamois climbs too, but has only short little horns. The ibex is the heraldic animal of the canton of the Grisons.
4514.m: The ibex climbs in the mountains.

4573.q: Which prey animals does the African wild dog often hunt?
4573.e: It hunts antelopes such as impalas and sometimes young wildebeest too. The prey depends on the area.
4573.m: Impalas and wildebeest are on the menu.

4608.q: Which family does the African wild dog belong to?
4608.e: It belongs to the dog family (Canidae). Despite its looks, it is not closely related to hyenas.
4608.m: Wild dogs belong to the dog family.

4674.q: What do you call animals that, like the wild dog, hunt and eat other animals?
4674.e: Predators feed on other animals that they hunt. The wild dog is one of them.

4722.q: Which animal is shown on the flag of Wales?
4722.e: The red dragon has been the symbol of Wales for centuries. It can be seen on the flag on a green and white background.

4739.q: The brown trout is cold-blooded. What does that mean?
a: Its body temperature adjusts to the water
Its body temperature is always 37 degrees
4739.e: Cold-blooded animals produce hardly any heat of their own. When the water is cold, their body works more slowly.
4739.m: In the cold-blooded brown trout, body temperature adjusts to the water.

4797.q: Which animal is shown on the coat of arms of the canton of Schaffhausen?
4797.e: The coat of arms of Schaffhausen shows a black ram rearing up on a gold background. The town's name, though, actually comes from “Schiffshausen”, meaning boat houses.

4821.q: How do adult wild dogs often bring food to the pups?
a: They bring up meat for them
They put fruit in the nest
4821.e: The adults bring up half-digested meat. This way the pups and the guards at the den are fed too.
4821.m: The pack shares food with the young.

4825.q: In the photo you can see a spawning pit. How is it made?
a: The female beats a hollow in the gravel with her tail
Beavers dig it for the fish
The male builds it from twigs
It forms when rain churns up the stream
4825.e: The female beats a pit into the gravel bed with her tail. There she lays her eggs and then covers them up again.
4825.m: The female beats pits into the gravel.

4832.q: In a wild dog pack, who often gets to eat first?
4832.e: In wild dogs, the pups are often allowed to eat first. This is a special kind of social behaviour.
4832.m: In wild dogs, the young often eat first.

4942.q: In the photo, the brown trout can hardly be seen on the gravel bed. What is its colouring for?
4942.e: The colours and spots match the bottom of the stream. So the trout is hard to see and can take prey by surprise.

4998.q: There are no lions or tigers in Sri Lanka. So what is the Sri Lankan leopard on the island?
a: The biggest wild cat on the island
An animal that only lives in zoos now
4998.e: Because there are no lions or tigers in Sri Lanka, the Sri Lankan leopard is the biggest wild cat on the island. It is at the top of the food chain.
4998.m: In Sri Lanka the leopard is the biggest wild cat.

5018.q: Which country has a red maple leaf on its flag?
5018.e: The maple leaf is Canada's best-known symbol and has been on the flag since 1965. Maple trees grow there in huge forests.
5018.m: Canada has a red maple leaf.

5042.q: Which water temperature does the brown trout like best?
a: Water that is frozen in winter
5042.e: The brown trout is a cold-water fish. If the water gets too warm, it gets stressed and there is too little oxygen.
5042.m: The brown trout is a cold-water fish.

5064.q: What does a minimum size mean in fishing?
a: A minimum length a fish must reach before it may be caught
The lowest allowed weight of the fishing line
5064.e: Smaller fish must be put back gently into the water. That way they can grow and breed later.
5064.m: Fish that are too small stay in the water.

5146.q: What do you call a protected area where animals such as the wild dog live safely?
5146.e: In national parks, animals and their habitats are protected. Wild dogs can live there undisturbed too.
5146.m: National parks protect animals and habitats.

5172.q: Why do scientists give animals such as the brown trout a Latin name?
a: So that they have the same name all over the world
Because Latin is shorter than English
So that nobody understands the name
Because the animals come from Italy
5172.e: The brown trout has a different name in every language. But the Latin name Salmo trutta fario is used everywhere, so scientists worldwide know which animal is meant.
5172.m: Latin names are valid all over the world.

5180.q: Roughly how old does a leopard get in the wild?
5180.e: In the wild, leopards usually live 12 to 17 years. In zoos they can live longer.
5180.m: Wild leopards live to about 15 years.

5185.q: When are African wild dogs usually active?
a: Mainly in the morning and evening
Only in the middle of the night
5185.e: They usually hunt in the cooler morning and evening hours. At midday they often rest in the shade.
5185.m: Wild dogs hunt at dawn and dusk.

5352.q: You see a leopard and a cheetah. How can you recognise the cheetah?
a: By the black tear stripes on its face
5352.e: Cheetahs have black lines running from the eyes to the mouth and simple spots on their fur. Leopards have rosettes.
5352.m: The cheetah has tear stripes on its face, the leopard has rosettes in its fur.

5386.q: Which animal is an enemy that often tries to take the wild dogs' prey?
5386.e: Lions and spotted hyenas sometimes steal the wild dogs' prey. Lions can also kill wild dogs.
5386.m: Lions and hyenas are rivals of wild dogs.

5467.q: How successful are African wild dogs at hunting compared with lions?
5467.e: Wild dogs are among the most successful hunters in Africa. Their teamwork and stamina pay off.
5467.m: Wild dogs are very successful hunters.

5581.q: What do you call a group of African wild dogs?
5581.e: Wild dogs live in packs. A pack usually consists of related animals.
5581.m: Wild dogs live in a pack.

5662.q: Which big cat is the only one that usually lives in groups called prides?
5662.e: Lions live in prides with several females, their young and one or a few males. Tigers, leopards and jaguars are loners.
5662.m: The lion is the only big cat that lives in a pride.

5672.q: Which trout originally comes from North America and is now often kept on fish farms?
5672.e: The rainbow trout was brought to Europe from North America. It grows quickly and is therefore often farmed. Brown trout, lake trout and sea trout are native here.
5672.m: The rainbow trout comes from North America.

5688.q: Roughly how heavy does an adult African wild dog get?
5688.e: It is about as heavy as a medium-sized dog. The animals are slim and long-legged.
5688.m: Wild dogs weigh about 20 to 30 kilograms.

5722.q: The picture shows a habitat. Where does the brown trout feel most at home?
a: In a cool, clear stream with lots of oxygen
In a swamp with no current
5722.e: The brown trout needs clean, cold water rich in oxygen. It finds such conditions in fast-flowing streams.
5722.m: It loves cool, clear, fast streams.

5749.q: How many pups are often in an African wild dog litter?
a: Often more than six, sometimes over ten
5749.e: Wild dogs have quite large litters. The number of pups can even be over ten.

5758.e: Fish eggs are called roe. Milt is the name for the males' sperm.

5807.q: Which country has a red circle in the middle of a white flag?
5807.e: The red circle on the Japanese flag represents the rising sun. That is why Japan is also called the “Land of the Rising Sun”.
5807.m: Japan's flag shows a red sun.

5843.q: What is special about the African wild dog's paws compared with many other dogs?
a: They have four toes on the front paws
5843.e: The wild dog has no fifth toe, the so-called dewclaw, on its front paws. So it has four toes there.
5843.m: Wild dogs have only four toes at the front.

5881.q: What does the African wild dog mainly eat?
5881.e: It is a meat-eater and mainly hunts medium-sized antelopes such as impalas. Smaller prey is also on the menu.
5881.m: Wild dogs are meat-eaters and hunt antelopes.

5908.q: What makes the wild dog a good long-distance runner?
5908.e: It can chase its prey over long distances. This tires out the prey animals.
5908.m: Wild dogs hunt with lots of stamina.

5940.q: You see a brown trout. Which family of fish does it belong to?
5940.e: The brown trout belongs to the salmon family. Its relatives include the salmon and the rainbow trout.
5940.m: The brown trout is in the salmon family.

5956.q: What is one difference between a leopard and a jaguar?
a: The jaguar is more powerfully built
The leopard lives in South America
5956.e: The jaguar looks bulkier and has a bigger head. It also lives in America, while the leopard lives in Africa and Asia.
5956.m: The jaguar is stockier, the leopard slimmer.

6009.q: In the photo a leopard is lying on a branch. What does it often do with its prey in the tree?
a: It hides it and eats it there
It throws it into the water
6009.e: Leopards are strong climbers and drag their prey up trees. This protects it from lions and hyenas.
6009.m: Leopards take their prey up trees.

6121.q: Which animal is the national symbol and heraldic animal of the USA?
6121.e: The bald eagle was declared the national symbol of the USA in 1782 and appears on the country's Great Seal. It stands for strength and freedom.
6121.m: The USA has the bald eagle as its symbol.

6133.q: How does a male leopard usually differ from a female?
a: It has stripes instead of spots
6133.e: Male leopards are usually much heavier than females. They can weigh about 60 to 90 kilograms.

6163.q: How can you tell individual leopards apart in camera trap pictures?
a: By the spot pattern, which is different for each one
By the size of their ears
By the colour of their eyes
6163.e: Every leopard's spot pattern is unique, a bit like a fingerprint. Researchers use this to count the animals.

6189.q: Is the snow leopard a subspecies of the leopard?
a: No, it is a separate species
Yes, a subspecies from the Himalayas
Yes, a subspecies with light fur
No, it belongs to the lynxes
6189.e: The snow leopard is called Panthera uncia and is a separate species. It is related to the leopard, but it is not the same animal. It is not a lynx either.
6189.m: The snow leopard is a separate species.

6203.e: Leopards usually hunt at dusk and at night. During the day they often rest in the shade or in trees.

6217.q: Because of its coat, what else is the African wild dog called?
6217.e: The name hyena dog comes from its spotted appearance and its hunched walk, which is reminiscent of hyenas. But it is not related to hyenas.
6217.m: Hyena dog is another name for it.

6236.q: In which part of Africa does the African wild dog mainly live today?
a: In the middle of the Sahara
6236.e: The African wild dog lives mainly in the savannahs south of the Sahara, for example in Botswana, Tanzania and Zimbabwe. Today it is only found in small areas.
6236.m: The wild dog lives in Africa's savannahs south of the Sahara.

6348.q: Which animals are the “Big Five” in Africa?
6348.e: The Big Five are the lion, leopard, elephant, rhino and buffalo. They used to be seen as especially hard to hunt; today they are mostly photographed.
6348.m: The leopard is one of the Big Five.

6363.q: Which insect, whose larva lives in streams, is a favourite food of trout?
6363.e: Larvae of mayflies, stoneflies and caddisflies live in streams. They are important food for trout.

6382.q: In fly fishing for trout, an artificial fly is often used. What is it made of?
a: Feathers and thread, copying an insect
Shiny metal, shaped like a spoon
6382.e: Fly fishers tie small copies of insects out of feathers, hair and thread. They use them to fool hungry trout.

6464.q: Which feature of the brown trout can you see particularly well in the photo?
a: Red spots with a pale ring
A big black spot on the tail
6464.e: The brown trout has red and black spots on its skin. The red spots are often surrounded by a pale ring.
6464.m: Red spots with a pale ring

6477.q: What is one feature of the African wild dog's coat?
a: Each animal has a different pattern
It is the same plain colour on all of them
6477.e: The patches of black, yellow, brown and white are different on every animal. This makes it possible to recognise individual animals.
6477.m: No two wild dogs look the same.

6549.q: Where does the Amur leopard you see in the photo live?
a: In the east of Russia and the north-east of China
6549.e: The Amur leopard lives in forests in the Russian Far East and neighbouring China. It is one of the rarest big cats in the world.
6549.m: Amur leopards live in the Far East.

6697.q: Which small crustacean, living under stones in streams, is eaten by brown trout?
6697.e: The freshwater shrimp is only about 1 to 2 centimetres long. It lives in clean streams and is common prey.
6697.m: The freshwater shrimp is a popular food.

6709.q: The brook trout looks similar to the brown trout. Where does it originally come from?
6709.e: The brook trout came to Europe from North America. It is a char and does not belong to the trout genus.
6709.m: The brook trout comes from North America.

6749.q: Which animal has black and white stripes and lives in Africa?
6749.e: Every zebra has a unique stripe pattern, almost like a fingerprint. Zebras live in herds on the savannah.
6749.m: Zebras have black and white stripes.

6789.q: What makes the brown trout different from the Atlantic salmon?
a: It usually stays in fresh water and in the stream
It always lives in the sea
6789.e: The salmon migrates to the sea to feed and returns to spawn. The brown trout usually spends its life in the stream.
6789.m: The brown trout usually stays in the stream.

6878.q: The picture shows a rainbow trout with a pink band. Where does it originally come from?
6878.e: The rainbow trout was brought to Europe from North America. The brown trout, on the other hand, is native to Europe.
6878.m: The rainbow trout comes from North America.

7105.q: What is a leopard especially good at?
7105.e: With strong legs and claws, the leopard climbs trees skilfully. It can even climb up with prey in its mouth.

7188.q: Which big cat lives in America and has rosettes with dots in the middle?
7188.e: The jaguar looks like the leopard but lives in America. Its rosettes usually have one or more dots inside.
7188.m: The jaguar lives in America, the leopard does not.

7323.q: How does the wild dog look different from a pet dog?
a: Its coat is patchy and its ears are big
Its coat is made of feathers
7323.e: The wild dog has a colourful patchy pattern and big, round ears. It also has no dewclaw at the front.
7323.m: Patches and big ears stand out.

7402.q: Roughly how heavy can an adult male leopard get?
7402.e: Males usually weigh between 60 and 90 kilograms. That is about as much as an adult human.
7402.m: Male leopards weigh up to about 90 kilos.

7512.q: How does an adult brown trout usually behave towards other trout?
a: It lives in a huge shoal
It swims to the sea every day
7512.e: Brown trout are often loners and stay in one good spot. Intruders are driven away.

7523.q: Why is there a closed season for brown trout?
a: So that they can spawn undisturbed
Because the water is too cold for fishing then
7523.e: During the closed season they must not be caught. This keeps the next generation safe.

7564.q: What are the young of the African wild dog called?
7564.e: As with other dogs, the young are called pups. They are born in a den.
7564.m: Young wild dogs are called pups.

7575.q: Which animals is the leopard most closely related to?
7575.e: Leopards, lions, tigers and jaguars belong to the same genus of big cats. A typical feature is that they can roar.
7575.m: Leopards, lions, tigers and jaguars are closely related big cats.

7579.q: Which animal is shown on the coat of arms of the canton of Bern?
7579.e: The bear is the heraldic animal of Bern and even gave the city its name. The story goes that the founder chose the first animal he killed for it.
7579.m: Bern has a bear on its coat of arms.

7582.q: What does a leopard's typical call often sound like?
7582.e: The leopard's call is often compared to the sound of a saw. It uses it to get attention.
7582.m: The leopard's call sounds like sawing.

7593.q: Experts divide streams and rivers into sections according to typical fish. What is the upper, cool and fast-flowing section called?
7593.e: In the cool, oxygen-rich upper course, trout are the main fish. That is why this section is called the trout zone.
7593.m: The trout zone is in the upper course.

7735.q: Which country has a flag that, apart from its proportions, looks almost exactly like the flag of Monaco?
7735.e: The flags of Indonesia and Monaco both consist of a red and a white stripe, but they differ in their proportions. Indonesia has used its flag since independence in 1945.
7735.m: Indonesia and Monaco have almost identical flags.

7815.q: Why is a hot summer dangerous for brown trout?
a: The prey animals get too big
7815.e: The warmer the water, the less oxygen it can hold. For cold-water fish it then becomes life-threatening.

7863.q: In the dish “trout au bleu”, the trout's skin turns bluish. Where does this colour come from?
a: The layer of slime reacts with vinegar
The trout is dyed with food colouring
7863.e: The trout is cooked fresh, with its layer of slime, in a vinegar stock. This turns the skin bluish.
7863.m: Vinegar turns the slime layer blue.

8072.q: What colour is the cross on the Swiss flag?
8072.e: The Swiss flag shows a white cross on a red background. It is one of the oldest flags in the world.
8072.m: The Swiss flag shows a white cross on a red background.

8106.q: The sea trout is the same species as the brown trout. What does it do differently?
a: It migrates to the sea and returns to rivers to spawn
It only lives in mountain lakes
8106.e: The sea trout feeds in the sea and grows bigger there. To spawn, it swims into rivers and streams.
8106.m: Sea trout spawn in fresh water.

8112.q: Which animal sits on a cactus in the centre of the Mexican coat of arms?
8112.e: Mexico's coat of arms shows an eagle sitting on a cactus and eating a snake. It goes back to an Aztec founding legend.
8112.m: Mexico's coat of arms shows an eagle with a snake.

8146.q: Which statement about the Persian leopard is true?
a: It lives mainly in the Caucasus and Iran
It only lives in South America
It lives at the North Pole
8146.e: The Persian leopard is a subspecies found in Western Asia, for example in Iran and the Caucasus. It is one of the biggest subspecies.
8146.m: The Persian leopard lives in Western Asia.

8226.q: How do leopards usually move around?
a: On four paws, quietly and smoothly
8226.e: Leopards walk on soft paws into which they can pull their claws. This lets them move almost silently.

8250.q: How does the African wild dog usually hunt?
a: As a team in a pack
Only at night in the water
8250.e: The animals hunt together and often chase their prey for a long time. Thanks to their teamwork they are very successful.
8250.m: Hunting together makes wild dogs successful.

8267.q: What are young leopards like straight after birth?
a: Almost as big as their mother
8267.e: Newborn leopards are blind and must be hidden and cared for by their mother. They only open their eyes after a few days.

8268.q: Which animal is shown on the coat of arms of the canton of Appenzell Ausserrhoden?
8268.e: Like Appenzell Innerrhoden, Appenzell Ausserrhoden also has an upright black bear on its coat of arms. The two cantons used to be a single canton of Appenzell.
8268.m: Ausserrhoden also has a bear on its coat of arms.

8289.q: Which large bird often stands motionless in the water and catches trout?
8289.e: The grey heron waits quietly in shallow water. Then it strikes like lightning with its long beak.
8289.m: The grey heron lies in wait in shallow water.

8398.q: How do wild dogs mainly find their prey?
a: With heat sensors on their paws
8398.e: They use their senses, especially their good eyesight in open country. Then the pack chases the prey.
8398.m: Their senses help wild dogs hunt.

8458.q: What helps brown trout when a stream is restored to its natural state?
8458.e: Gravel beds serve as spawning sites, and roots and stones as hiding places. A straightened concrete stream, on the other hand, offers hardly any habitat.

8510.q: Why is pack size important for the wild dog?
a: Large packs hunt and protect better
8510.e: In a bigger pack, more animals can hunt and guard the pups. Defending against enemies also works better.

8632.q: Where is the brown trout originally native?
8632.e: The brown trout originally comes from Europe. Later, people took it to many other countries.

8653.q: The photo shows a snow leopard. Where does it live?
a: In the high mountains of Central Asia
8653.e: The snow leopard lives in high mountains such as the Himalayas. It is a separate species, not a subspecies of the leopard.
8653.m: Snow leopards live in the mountains of Central Asia.

8674.q: Which of these animals is prey for a leopard?
8674.e: The impala is a medium-sized antelope and fits the leopard's choice of prey well. Adult elephants and rhinos are far too big.

8683.q: What is it called when trout swim to their spawning grounds?
8683.e: At spawning time, trout often move upstream to gravelly spots. There must be no obstacles in the way.
8683.m: The spawning migration leads to the spawning ground.

8689.q: What is a female leopard called?
8689.e: The female is called a leopardess. The male is simply called a leopard.
8689.m: The female is called a leopardess.

8738.q: When do brown trout normally spawn?
a: Only at full moon in July
8738.e: Unlike many other fish, the brown trout lays its eggs in autumn and winter. The young fish then hatch in winter or spring.
8738.m: Brown trout spawn in autumn and winter.

8772.q: Which group of vertebrates does the leopard belong to?
8772.e: Leopards have fur, give birth to live young and feed them with milk. These are typical features of mammals.

8825.q: What is on the brown trout's menu?
8825.e: The brown trout eats animals such as insect larvae, freshwater shrimps, worms and small fish. It also snaps up insects that fall onto the water.
8825.m: It eats insects, crustaceans and small fish.

8853.q: Which is the only country in the world with a triangular rather than rectangular national flag?
8853.e: Nepal is the only country in the world with an official national flag that is not rectangular. It consists of two triangles, one above the other.
8853.m: Nepal is the only country without a rectangular flag.

8940.q: What does the leopard in the picture like to eat most?
8940.e: The leopard is a meat-eater. It mainly catches medium-sized hoofed animals such as antelopes, but smaller animals too.

9026.q: How many golden stars are on the flag of the European Union?
9026.e: The EU flag shows twelve golden stars in a circle on a blue background, regardless of the number of member states. Twelve stands for completeness and unity.
9026.m: The EU flag always has 12 stars.

9083.q: What does the presence of brown trout tell you about a stream?
a: The water is clean and rich in oxygen
The water is full of mud
9083.e: The brown trout needs very good water quality. That is why it shows that a stream is healthy.
9083.m: Trout are a sign of clean water.

9106.q: Which country has a red and blue Taegeuk symbol, similar to yin and yang, in the centre of its flag?
9106.e: The South Korean flag shows the red and blue Taegeuk symbol in the middle, which stands for harmony. Four black trigrams are arranged around it.
9106.m: South Korea shows the Taegeuk symbol.

9168.q: Who composed the famous song “The Trout” (“Die Forelle”)?
9168.e: In 1817 Franz Schubert set to music a poem about a trout in a stream. Later he also wrote the “Trout Quintet”.

9254.q: Which animal family does the leopard in the picture belong to?
9254.e: The leopard is a predator from the cat family. Within it, it counts as one of the big cats.
9254.m: The leopard is a big cat.

9263.q: What is particularly harmful to brown trout in a stream?
a: Sewage and fertiliser, which use up oxygen
9263.e: Polluted water often contains less oxygen and also toxic substances. Trout cannot cope with that well.

9347.q: How can experts tell the age of a trout?
a: By the annual rings on its scales
By the colour of its eyes
By the length of its snout
9347.e: Rings form on the scales, similar to trees. In winter they grow more slowly, which you can see under a microscope.

9422.q: Which colourful bird dives for small fish, including young trout?
9422.e: The kingfisher sits on a branch by the water and plunges down onto its prey. Its feathers shimmer blue and orange.

9503.q: Some river power stations have a fish ladder made of many small pools. What is it for?
a: Fish can use it to get past weirs
Fish spend the winter in it
It keeps birds of prey away
9503.e: A fish ladder consists of small steps with pools. This lets fish swim upstream past weirs and dams.
9503.m: Fish ladders help fish over obstacles.

9527.q: Which sounds do African wild dogs use to communicate, among others?
9527.e: Wild dogs twitter and squeak to communicate. They also use body language.
9527.m: Wild dogs communicate with squeaks and calls.

9574.q: Which endangered animal lives in the wild only in China and eats almost nothing but bamboo?
9574.e: The giant panda lives in the mountain forests of China and feeds almost entirely on bamboo. Thanks to conservation programmes, its numbers have recently recovered slightly.
9574.m: Pandas live in the wild only in China.

9618.q: In the picture a trout is hiding. Where does it like to stay?
a: Under stones, roots and overhanging banks
On dry land on the bank
In the middle of a bare concrete slab
9618.e: Such hiding places protect it from enemies and from the strong current. It also lies in wait for prey from there.
9618.m: It hides under stones and roots.

9658.q: Trout have a small extra fin without bony rays on their back, just before the tail fin. What is it called?
9658.e: Fish of the salmon family such as the brown trout have a small adipose fin in addition to the dorsal fin. It has no bony rays.
9658.m: Salmon-family fish have a small adipose fin.

13064.q: On which continent was ancient Egypt?
13064.e: Egypt lies in the north-east of Africa. The kingdom of the pharaohs arose there about 5000 years ago.

13065.q: What is the capital of Egypt today?
13065.e: Cairo lies on the Nile and is Egypt's largest city. The Pyramids of Giza are close by.
13065.m: The capital of Egypt is Cairo.

13066.q: What kind of landscape covers most of Egypt?
13066.e: Almost all of Egypt is desert. Only along the Nile is there enough water for fields and villages.

13067.q: Which cereals did farmers in ancient Egypt mainly grow?
13067.e: The Egyptians mainly grew wheat and barley. They used the grain to bake bread, for example.
13067.m: Egyptian farmers mainly grew wheat and barley.

13068.q: Which drink did the ancient Egyptians make from barley?
13068.e: Beer was an everyday drink in ancient Egypt. It was brewed from barley and bread.
13068.m: The Egyptians brewed beer from barley.

13069.q: Which animal was especially loved and respected by the ancient Egyptians?
13069.e: Cats caught mice and snakes. They were even considered sacred animals of a goddess.
13069.m: The cat was highly respected in ancient Egypt.

13070.q: What did most Egyptians build their houses from?
13070.e: The houses were made of bricks of Nile mud, dried in the sun. Stone was mainly used for temples and tombs.
13070.m: Houses in Egypt were built of mud bricks.

13071.q: What fabric were the clothes of the ancient Egyptians usually made of?
13071.e: Linen is made from the flax plant. The light fabric was pleasant in the heat.
13071.m: The Egyptians usually wore light linen clothes.

13072.q: What was a popular board game of the ancient Egyptians called?
13072.e: Senet was played on a board with 30 squares. Senet games have even been found in tombs.
13072.m: The ancient Egyptians liked playing the board game Senet.

13073.q: Which animal often carried heavy loads in ancient Egypt?
13073.e: Donkeys were the most important pack animals. Camels only became common in Egypt much later.
13073.m: In ancient Egypt, donkeys carried heavy loads.

13074.q: Roughly how long did the kingdom of the pharaohs last?
13074.e: The kingdom of the pharaohs began about 5000 years ago. It only ended when the Romans conquered Egypt.
13074.m: The kingdom of the pharaohs lasted about 3000 years.

13075.q: What do you call researchers who dig old things out of the ground?
13075.e: Archaeologists carefully dig up tombs, houses and objects. This teaches us a lot about ancient Egypt.
13075.m: Archaeologists dig up and study old things.

13076.q: What is the great river that flows through Egypt called?
13076.e: The Nile flows from south to north through the whole of Egypt. Without it, hardly anyone could live there.
13076.m: The great river in Egypt is the Nile.

13077.q: What is true about the length of the Nile?
a: It is one of the longest rivers in the world
It is the shortest river in Africa
It is shorter than the Aare
It is only as long as a lake
13077.e: Depending on how it is measured, the Nile is over 6500 kilometres long. Together with the Amazon, it is one of the longest rivers on Earth.
13077.m: The Nile is one of the longest rivers in the world.

13078.q: Into which sea does the Nile flow?
13078.e: The Nile flows into the Mediterranean in the north of Egypt. Before that, it splits into several branches.
13078.m: The Nile flows into the Mediterranean.

13079.q: What happened on the Nile every year in late summer in ancient Egypt?
13079.e: Heavy rains far to the south, in the highlands of Ethiopia, made the Nile swell every year. Then it flooded the fields along its banks.
13079.m: Every year the Nile flooded the fields.

13080.q: What did the Nile flood leave behind on the fields?
13080.e: The dark mud was a good fertiliser. Grain grew especially well on it.
13080.m: The flood brought fertile mud to the fields.

13081.q: The ancient Egyptians called their land ‘Kemet’. What does that mean?
13081.e: The name comes from the dark mud of the Nile. The desert, on the other hand, they called ‘red land’.
13081.m: Kemet means ‘black land’ because of the dark Nile mud.

13082.q: Which dangerous animal lived in the Nile?
13082.e: Many crocodiles lived in the Nile. People feared them and even worshipped a crocodile god.
13082.m: Dangerous crocodiles lived in the Nile.

13083.q: In German, which large animal has the river's name in its own name?
13083.e: In German the hippo is called ‘Nilpferd’, meaning ‘Nile horse’. Hippos live in rivers and lakes in Africa, and in ancient Egypt there were also hippos on the Nile.
13083.m: In German the hippo is named after the Nile.

13084.q: How did the ancient Egyptians move grain and large stones over long distances?
13084.e: The Nile was Egypt's most important road. Boats carried people, grain and even large stones from place to place.
13084.m: The Egyptians travelled by boat on the Nile.

13085.q: How did farmers bring Nile water to their fields?
13085.e: The farmers dug canals from the river to the fields. This way the plants had enough water even after the flood.
13085.m: Canals carried Nile water to the fields.

13086.q: Where did most people live in ancient Egypt?
a: On the banks of the Nile
In the middle of the desert
13086.e: Only along the Nile was there water and fertile soil. That is why almost all villages and towns were on the river.
13086.m: Most Egyptians lived on the banks of the Nile.

13087.q: What is the area called where the Nile splits into several branches before reaching the sea?
13087.e: The Nile Delta is shaped like a triangle. It looks like the Greek letter delta.
13087.m: Before the sea, the Nile splits into several branches in the delta.

13088.q: Which plant grew on the banks of the Nile and was very useful?
13088.e: Papyrus is a kind of reed. The Egyptians used it to make writing sheets, baskets, ropes and even boats.
13088.m: The useful papyrus plant grew along the Nile.

13090.q: What did the word ‘pharaoh’ originally mean?
13090.e: At first the word meant the royal palace. Later the king himself was called that.

13091.q: What did the ancient Egyptians believe about their pharaoh?
a: He is like a god on earth
He is a servant of the priests
He is a soldier like all the others
13091.e: The pharaoh was regarded as the son of the sun god. He was supposed to keep order in the land.
13091.m: The Egyptians saw the pharaoh as a god on earth.

13092.q: What did the pharaoh often wear on his head?
13092.e: The striped headcloth is called a nemes. You can also see it on the famous death mask of Tutankhamun.
13092.m: The pharaoh often wore a striped headcloth.

13093.q: What did the pharaoh wear on his chin at festivals?
13093.e: The false beard was a sign of royal dignity. It was fastened with straps.
13093.m: The pharaoh wore a false beard as a sign of his power.

13094.q: What did the pharaoh hold in his hands as a sign of his power?
13094.e: The crook is like a shepherd's staff. It shows that the pharaoh leads his people like a shepherd leads his flock.
13094.m: The crook and flail were signs of the pharaoh's power.

13095.q: Which animal sat on the front of the pharaoh's crown to protect him?
13095.e: The rearing cobra on the forehead was meant to frighten enemies away. It was a protective symbol of the king.
13095.m: A cobra on the crown protected the pharaoh.

13096.q: From how many parts was Egypt first united into one kingdom?
13096.e: There was Upper Egypt in the south and Lower Egypt in the north. That is why the pharaoh was also called ‘Lord of the Two Lands’.
13096.m: Egypt was formed from two parts, Upper and Lower Egypt.

13097.q: Which famous queen was the last to rule Egypt before the Romans conquered it?
13097.e: Cleopatra was the last queen of independent Egypt. When the Romans conquered Egypt, she died, and Egypt became part of the Roman Empire.
13097.m: Cleopatra was the last queen of ancient Egypt before the Romans.

13098.q: Which woman ruled as pharaoh herself and had a great terraced temple built near Luxor?
13098.e: Hatshepsut ruled as pharaoh for about 20 years. Her temple at Deir el-Bahari has three large terraces in front of a cliff.
13098.m: Hatshepsut was a woman who ruled as pharaoh herself.

13099.q: Which pharaoh ruled for a very long time and had the rock temples of Abu Simbel built?
13099.e: Ramesses II ruled for about 66 years. In front of his temple at Abu Simbel sit four giant statues of him.
13099.m: Ramesses II had the temples of Abu Simbel built.

13100.q: What is the valley where many pharaohs were buried in rock tombs called?
13100.e: The Valley of the Kings is near the city of Luxor. There the Egyptians dug deep tombs into the rock.
13100.m: Many pharaohs are buried in the Valley of the Kings.

13101.q: Which queen, the wife of the pharaoh Akhenaten, is famous for a painted bust?
13101.e: The colourful bust of Nefertiti is over 3000 years old. Today it is in a museum in Berlin.
13101.m: The bust of Queen Nefertiti is world-famous.

13102.q: What were the great pyramids built for?
13102.e: Pharaohs were buried in the pyramids. They were meant to secure their way into the afterlife.
13102.m: The pyramids were tombs for pharaohs.

13103.q: On which side of the Nile did the Egyptians build most pyramids and tombs?
a: In the west, where the sun sets
In the east, where the sun rises
On islands in the middle of the Nile
13103.e: The Egyptians linked the west, where the sun sets, with the realm of the dead. That is why most pyramids and tombs are on the west bank of the Nile.
13103.m: Most pyramids and tombs are west of the Nile.

13104.q: How many great pyramids stand side by side at Giza?
13104.e: They are the pyramids of the pharaohs Khufu, Khafre and Menkaure. There are also a few small pyramids next to them.
13104.m: There are three great pyramids at Giza.

13105.q: What shape is the base of an Egyptian pyramid?
13105.e: The base is square. The four sides are triangles that meet at a point at the top.
13105.m: A pyramid has a square base.

13106.q: What were the great pyramids built from?
13106.e: The Great Pyramid of Khufu needed over two million stone blocks. Many of them are heavier than a car.
13106.m: The pyramids are made of huge stone blocks.

13107.q: Roughly how tall is the Great Pyramid of Khufu (Cheops)?
13107.e: It used to be almost 147 metres tall; today it is about 139 metres. That is roughly as tall as a 45-storey tower block.
13107.m: The Great Pyramid of Khufu is about 140 metres tall.

13108.q: What is special about the Great Pyramid of Khufu among the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World?
a: It is the only one still standing
13108.e: The other six wonders have been destroyed or have disappeared. Only the Great Pyramid of Khufu still exists.
13108.m: The Great Pyramid of Khufu is the only ancient wonder still standing.

13109.q: According to what we know today, who built the pyramids?
