14569.e: Asian goods reached Europe through many middlemen, for example in the Ottoman Empire and in Venice. Each trader added a mark-up, so the goods were very expensive.
14569.m: A sea route to Asia promised cheaper goods without middlemen.

14570.q: In which year did Vasco da Gama set off from Lisbon for India?
14570.e: The fleet left Lisbon in July 1497. After around ten months it reached India.
14570.m: Vasco da Gama set off from Lisbon in 1497.

14571.q: Who helped Vasco da Gama find his way from East Africa across the Indian Ocean to India?
14571.e: In the East African city of Malindi, Vasco da Gama took an experienced pilot on board. He knew the monsoon winds and the way to India.
14571.m: A pilot from East Africa showed Vasco da Gama the way across the Indian Ocean.

14572.q: Which Portuguese prince supported voyages of discovery along Africa early in the 15th century?
14572.e: From about 1420, Henry the Navigator sent ships along the African coast. This laid the foundation for the later voyages to India.
14572.m: Henry the Navigator laid the foundation for Portugal’s voyages of discovery.

14573.q: Which nimble type of ship was especially important for the Portuguese voyages of discovery?
14573.e: The caravel was small and fast and could also tack against the wind. That made it well suited to exploring unknown coasts.
14573.m: The caravel was a typical explorers’ ship.

14574.q: What did Vasco da Gama achieve on his voyage from 1497 to 1499?
a: He found the sea route from Europe to India
He was the first to sail around the Earth
14574.e: Vasco da Gama sailed around the southern tip of Africa and on across the Indian Ocean to India. This gave Portugal a sea route to the spices of Asia.
14574.m: Vasco da Gama found the sea route to India.

14575.q: Which country did Ferdinand Magellan come from?
14575.e: Magellan was Portuguese. Because his king, Manuel I, did not support him, he entered Spanish service.
14575.m: The Portuguese Magellan sailed for Spain.

14576.q: In which year did Magellan’s fleet set off on its voyage west?
14576.e: The fleet put to sea in September 1519 from the port of Sanlúcar de Barrameda in southern Spain. Before that it had been in Seville.

14577.q: With how many ships did Magellan’s expedition start?
14577.e: The five ships were called Trinidad, San Antonio, Concepción, Victoria and Santiago. Magellan’s flagship was the Trinidad.
14577.m: Magellan started out with five ships.

14578.q: Which sea passage at the southern tip of South America bears Magellan’s name?
14578.e: In 1520, Magellan found a passage between the mainland of South America and Tierra del Fuego. That is how he got from the Atlantic into the Pacific.
14578.m: Through the Strait of Magellan, Magellan reached the Pacific.

14948.q: In which year did the Catholic conservative cantons join together in the Sonderbund?
14948.e: In December 1845 seven Catholic conservative cantons founded a secret defensive alliance, the Sonderbund.

14949.q: Which of these cantons belonged to the Sonderbund?
14949.e: Lucerne was even the leading canton of the Sonderbund. Zurich, Bern and Aargau were on the liberal side.
14949.m: Lucerne was the most important canton in the Sonderbund.

14950.q: How many cantons made up the Sonderbund?
14950.e: Seven Catholic conservative cantons joined together. Obwalden and Nidwalden counted together as one canton (Unterwalden).
14950.m: Seven Catholic cantons formed the Sonderbund.

14951.q: Which of these cantons was NOT a member of the Sonderbund?
14951.e: Ticino was Catholic but did not join the Sonderbund. Valais, Fribourg and Zug were members.
14951.m: Catholic Ticino stayed out of the Sonderbund.

14952.q: What did the cantons of the Sonderbund mainly have in common?
a: They were all on Lake Geneva.
14952.e: The Sonderbund cantons were strongly Catholic and wanted to protect their old order and the rights of the Church.
14952.m: The Sonderbund was an alliance of Catholic conservative cantons.

14953.q: Who were the political opponents of the Sonderbund?
14953.e: The Liberals and Radicals (later the Free Democrats) wanted a stronger federal state and were in power in most cantons.
14953.m: Liberals and Radicals fought against the Sonderbund.

14954.q: Which dispute stirred up strong feelings in 1841 and helped lead to the Sonderbund?
a: The closing of the monasteries in Aargau
The building of the Gotthard Tunnel
The founding of ETH in Zurich
14954.e: In 1841 the canton of Aargau closed its monasteries. For the Catholic cantons this was an attack on their religion.
14954.m: The Aargau monastery dispute sharpened the conflict before the Sonderbund.

14955.q: Which religious order did Lucerne bring to its higher schools in 1844, angering the Liberals?
14955.e: The Liberals saw the appointment of the Jesuits in Lucerne as a provocation, and it led to raids by volunteer corps against Lucerne.
14955.m: Bringing the Jesuits to Lucerne greatly inflamed the dispute.

14956.q: What were the armed groups of Liberals called that marched against Lucerne in 1844 and 1845?
14956.e: Freischaren were volunteer, unofficial troops of Liberals and Radicals. Their attacks on Lucerne failed.
14956.m: The Freischaren raids on Lucerne failed in 1844 and 1845.

14957.q: What did the Sonderbund cantons want to prevent?
14957.e: The Sonderbund cantons wanted to keep their independence and the rights of the Church. They rejected a strong federal state.
14957.m: The Sonderbund was against a strong federal state.

14958.q: Why did the majority of the Diet consider the Sonderbund not allowed?
a: It broke the Federal Treaty of 1815.
It had no name of its own.
14958.e: The Federal Treaty of 1815 banned alliances between cantons that harmed the Confederation or other cantons. That is why the majority demanded that it be dissolved.
14958.m: The majority of the Diet saw the Sonderbund as a breach of the Federal Treaty.

14959.q: What did the majority of the Diet demand of the Sonderbund in 1847?
14959.e: After Geneva and St Gallen had become liberal, the Diet decided in July 1847 that the Sonderbund must be dissolved.
14959.m: In 1847 the Diet demanded that the Sonderbund be dissolved.

14960.q: Who came up with the name “Sonderbund” (separate alliance)?
14960.e: The members called their alliance a Protective Union. The Liberals called it the Sonderbund, and this name stuck.
14960.m: The name Sonderbund came from its opponents.

14961.q: In which year did the Sonderbund War take place?
14961.e: The Sonderbund War lasted from 3 to 29 November 1847.
14961.m: The Sonderbund War took place in November 1847.

14962.q: Who was general of the Confederate troops in the Sonderbund War?
14962.e: Guillaume-Henri Dufour from Geneva led the troops of the Diet. Henri Guisan was general in the Second World War.
14962.m: General Dufour led the Confederate army in the Sonderbund War.

14964.q: Which side won the Sonderbund War?
a: The Confederate troops of the Diet
Nobody, it ended in a draw
14964.e: The Confederate army was much larger and defeated the Sonderbund cantons within a few weeks.
14964.m: The troops of the Diet defeated the Sonderbund.

14965.q: Roughly how big was the Confederate army in the Sonderbund War?
14965.e: The Diet called up around 99,000 soldiers, the Sonderbund around 79,000.
14965.m: The Confederate army had almost 100,000 soldiers.

14967.q: Why did capturing Lucerne matter so much in the Sonderbund War?
a: Lucerne was the largest city in Europe
14967.e: Lucerne led the Sonderbund. Once Lucerne had been occupied on 24 November 1847, the Sonderbund had practically lost.
14967.m: With Lucerne the most important canton of the Sonderbund fell.

14968.q: Which city was occupied by the Confederate troops on 24 November 1847?
14968.e: After the defeats of 23 November, Lucerne, the leading canton of the Sonderbund, surrendered and troops occupied it.
14968.m: Once Lucerne had been occupied, the Sonderbund had practically lost.

14969.q: Which canton was the last to surrender, on 29 November 1847?
14969.e: Valais surrendered as the last Sonderbund canton. That ended the war.
14969.m: Valais surrendered last of all the Sonderbund cantons.

14970.q: What is the commander of the Confederate troops in the Sonderbund War especially known for?
a: He ordered prisoners and wounded to be treated humanely.
He changed sides to the Sonderbund.
He fought the war with aeroplanes.
14970.e: Dufour wanted a short war with as few victims as possible and demanded that the wounded, prisoners and civilians be spared.
14970.m: The Confederate general fought the war as gently as possible.

14971.q: Roughly how many deaths did the Sonderbund War cause?
14971.e: The figures vary: according to official numbers, around 150 people died and around 400 were wounded. Compared with other wars, the losses were small.
14971.m: The Sonderbund War caused relatively few deaths.

14972.q: What did the Diet decide on 4 November 1847?
a: To dissolve the Sonderbund by force
To make Bern the federal city
14972.e: After negotiations had failed, the Diet decided on 4 November 1847 to defeat the Sonderbund militarily.
14972.m: On 4 November 1847 the Diet decided on war against the Sonderbund.

14973.q: Why did the Sonderbund War end so quickly?
a: The Confederate army was larger and well led
14973.e: General Dufour led a larger army and acted quickly and to a plan. So the Sonderbund cantons were defeated within a few weeks.
14973.m: The superior Confederate army ended the war quickly.

14974.q: On which day did the Diet declare the new Federal Constitution accepted?
14974.e: On 12 September 1848 the Diet declared the Federal Constitution accepted. This day is seen as the birthday of the federal state.
14974.m: The first Federal Constitution was accepted on 12 September 1848.

14975.q: Which agreement was replaced by the Federal Constitution of 1848?
14975.e: The Federal Treaty of 1815 was a loose treaty between cantons. The Constitution of 1848 took its place.
14975.m: The Constitution of 1848 replaced the Federal Treaty of 1815.

14977.q: Which of these cantons rejected the Federal Constitution of 1848?
14977.e: It was rejected mainly by former Sonderbund cantons such as Uri, Schwyz, Obwalden, Nidwalden, Zug and Valais, plus Ticino and Appenzell Innerrhoden.
14977.m: Uri was one of the cantons that rejected the Constitution in 1848.

14978.q: Which country was the model for Switzerland’s two-chamber parliament?
14978.e: The two-chamber system, with a chamber of the people and a chamber of the member states, was based on the US Constitution. The chamber of the cantons corresponds to the Senate.
14978.m: The Swiss two-chamber system follows the example of the USA.

14979.q: What was abolished inside Switzerland by the Federal Constitution of 1848?
14979.e: Before, cantons collected customs duties at their borders. From 1848 there was a single economic area, and only the Confederation charged duties at the national border.
14979.m: Since 1848 there have been no customs duties between the cantons.

14980.q: Who was allowed to vote at federal level under the Constitution of 1848?
14980.e: In 1848 only men had the right to vote. Women only got it at federal level more than 120 years later.
14980.m: The Constitution of 1848 gave the vote only to men.

14981.q: Who did NOT at first have the freedom to settle anywhere in Switzerland under the Constitution of 1848?
14981.e: In 1848 the freedom of settlement applied only to Christian Swiss. Jews were given equal rights only later.
14981.m: The freedom of settlement of 1848 at first excluded Jews.

14982.q: Which cantons faced each other in the Sonderbund War before the Constitution of 1848?
14982.e: The liberal cantons wanted a stronger Confederation. The Catholic conservative cantons joined together in the Sonderbund and lost in 1847.
14982.m: In the Sonderbund War liberal cantons fought Catholic conservative cantons.

14983.q: What was the Confederation responsible for from 1848, instead of the cantons?
14983.e: In 1848 the Confederation was given only a few tasks, such as coinage, measures and weights, and foreign policy. Schools, police and criminal law stayed with the cantons.
14983.m: Since 1848 the Confederation has regulated coins, measures and weights, among other things.

14985.q: Since when has Switzerland’s current Federal Constitution been in force?
14985.e: The people and the cantons accepted the new Federal Constitution on 18 April 1999. It came into force on 1 January 2000.
14985.m: The current Federal Constitution has been in force since 2000.

14986.q: Which new government did the Federal Constitution of 1848 create?
14986.e: With the Constitution of 1848 Switzerland got a national government, the Federal Council. At that time it was elected for three years.
14986.m: Since 1848 the Federal Council has governed Switzerland.

14987.q: What is the form of state that Switzerland got in 1848 called?
14987.e: Before 1848 Switzerland was a loose confederation of states. From 1848 it was a federal state with a common government and a common parliament.
14987.m: Since 1848 Switzerland has been a federal state.

14988.q: What is the most important difference between a confederation of states and a federal state?
a: A federal state has a common government and a common parliament.
A confederation of states always has a king.
A federal state no longer has member states.
A confederation of states always has only one language.
14988.e: In a confederation of states the members stay largely independent. In a federal state there is also a central state with its own authorities.
14988.m: A federal state has its own common authorities.

14989.q: Which city did the Federal Assembly choose on 28 November 1848 as the seat of the federal authorities?
14989.e: Bern won the most votes in both chambers in the very first round. Since then Bern has been the seat of the Federal Council and Parliament.
14989.m: Bern has been the seat of the Federal Council and Parliament since 1848.

14990.q: Why is Bern called the “federal city” rather than the “capital”?
a: Because no capital is set down in law
Because Bern is the largest city
Because Bern is in the canton of Zurich
Because the king lives in Bern
14990.e: Legally, Switzerland has no capital. Bern is the seat of the federal authorities and is therefore called the federal city.
14990.m: Bern is the federal city of Switzerland.

14991.q: Which city was Bern’s strongest rival for the federal seat in 1848?
14991.e: In the National Council, Bern received 58 votes, Zurich 35 and Lucerne 6. Zurich also came second in the Council of States.
14991.m: Zurich lost to Bern in the race for the federal seat in 1848.

14992.q: Which important university did Zurich receive, in a way as compensation for not becoming the federal seat?
14992.e: Zurich became the home of the Swiss Federal Institute of Technology (ETH). Lausanne later received the Federal Supreme Court.
14992.m: Zurich received ETH as the federal university.

14993.q: In which year was the franc introduced as the single currency for all of Switzerland?
14993.e: With the Coinage Act of 7 May 1850 the Swiss franc became the common currency. Before that the cantons had many coins of their own.
14993.m: Since 1850 people have paid with francs throughout Switzerland.

14994.q: Which currency served as the model for the Swiss franc in 1850?
14994.e: The new franc followed the French silver franc. One franc has 100 centimes (Rappen).
14994.m: The Swiss franc was modelled on the French franc.

14995.q: How many cantons did Switzerland have when the federal state was founded in 1848?
14995.e: In 1848 there were 22 cantons, some of them split into half-cantons. Today Switzerland has 26 cantons.
14995.m: When the federal state was founded there were 22 cantons.

14996.q: Which canton was the youngest, joining only in 1979?
14996.e: The canton of Jura was created in 1979 by splitting off from the canton of Bern. It is the youngest canton in Switzerland.
14996.m: Jura has been the youngest canton since 1979.

14997.q: Which party had won the Sonderbund War and then governed the young federal state alone for decades?
14997.e: The Free Democrats (today the FDP) provided all members of the Federal Council until 1891. Only then did a Catholic conservative join.
14997.m: The Free Democrats governed the federal state alone in its first decades.

14998.q: In which year was 1 August celebrated as the national day for the first time?
14998.e: In 1891 people celebrated the 600th anniversary of the Confederation on 1 August. It has been celebrated every year since 1899, and since a popular vote in 1993 it has been a public holiday.
14998.m: 1 August was first celebrated as the national day in 1891.

14999.q: How many members does the Federal Council have?
14999.e: Since 1848 the Federal Council has had seven members with equal rights.
14999.m: The Federal Council has seven members.

15000.q: Who elects the members of the Federal Council?
a: The people at the ballot box
15000.e: The National Council and the Council of States elect the Federal Council together as the United Federal Assembly.

15001.q: For how many years is the Federal Council elected today?
15001.e: The members of the Federal Council are elected for four years, each time after the National Council elections.
15001.m: The Federal Council is elected for four years.

15002.q: How long is the term of office of the President of the Confederation?
15002.e: The presidency changes every year. The president chairs the meetings but is only first among equals.
15002.m: The presidency of the Confederation changes every year.

15003.q: What does the principle of collegiality in the Federal Council mean?
a: The Federal Council decides together and stands by its decisions together.
The people decide at every meeting.
15003.e: The members of the Federal Council support decisions together, even if they disagreed in private.
15003.m: The Federal Council stands by its decisions together.

15004.q: What does each member of the Federal Council lead?
15004.e: Each member of the Federal Council heads a department, for example the Department of Defence. The number of departments has stayed the same since 1848.
15004.m: Each member of the Federal Council heads a department.

15005.q: When was the first Federal Council elected?
15005.e: The newly elected Federal Assembly elected the first seven Federal Councillors on 16 November 1848.
15005.m: The first Federal Council was elected in November 1848.

15006.q: Who chairs the meetings of the Federal Council?
a: The President of the National Council
The President of the Federal Supreme Court
15006.e: The presidency changes every year. The president chairs the meetings. The first President of the Confederation, in 1848, was Jonas Furrer.
15006.m: The President of the Confederation chairs the Federal Council’s meetings.

15007.q: Which language region did Stefano Franscini represent in the first Federal Council of 1848?
15007.e: Stefano Franscini came from Ticino. He represented Italian-speaking Switzerland in the first Federal Council.
15007.m: Stefano Franscini was the first Federal Councillor from Ticino.

15008.q: Who was elected to the Federal Council in 1984 as the first woman?
15008.e: Elisabeth Kopp became a member on 2 October 1984. She was the first woman in the national government.
15008.m: In 1984 Elisabeth Kopp became the first woman Federal Councillor.

15009.q: What is the distribution of seats in the Federal Council that applied from 1959 called?
15009.e: From 1959 the FDP, CVP and SP each got two seats and the SVP one seat. In 2003 one CVP seat went to the SVP.
15009.m: From 1959 the magic formula shared the Federal Council seats among four parties.

15010.q: Which party got a seat in the Federal Council for the first time in 1943, with Ernst Nobs?
15010.e: Ernst Nobs was elected to the Federal Council on 15 December 1943 as the first Social Democrat.
15010.m: Ernst Nobs was the first SP Federal Councillor in 1943.

15011.q: What does concordance mean in Swiss politics?
a: As many major parties as possible take part in government.
The Federal Council is chosen by lot.
15011.e: Concordance is an unwritten principle: the big parties should all be represented together in the Federal Council.
15011.m: Concordance means that the big parties govern together.

15012.q: Who does the National Council represent first and foremost?
15012.e: The National Council is the chamber of the people. Its seats are shared out among the cantons according to population.
15012.m: The National Council represents the people.

15013.q: How are the 200 National Council seats shared out among the cantons?
a: Each canton gets the same number
According to the age of the canton
15013.e: Cantons with more people get more seats. But every canton is entitled to at least one seat.
15013.m: National Council seats depend on the population of the cantons.

15014.q: Which canton has the most seats in the National Council?
15014.e: Zurich is the canton with the largest population and had 36 seats in the 2023 elections.
15014.m: Zurich has the most members of the National Council.

15015.q: What is the minimum number of seats each canton has in the National Council?
15015.e: Even very small cantons such as Uri or Appenzell Innerrhoden have at least one seat in the National Council.
15015.m: Every canton has at least one seat in the National Council.

15016.q: How often is the National Council elected?
15016.e: The National Council is elected by the people every four years in October, most recently in October 2023.
15016.m: The National Council is elected every four years.

15017.q: Which voting system has been used to elect the National Council since 1919?
15017.e: Since 1919 the seats have been shared out in proportion to the parties’ votes. As a result the Free Democrats lost their absolute majority.
15017.m: Since 1919 the National Council has been elected by proportional representation.

15018.q: How many members does the National Council have today?
15018.e: The National Council has 200 members. Together with the 46 members of the Council of States, that makes 246 members of parliament.

15019.q: How many women were elected in 1971 as the first women members of the National Council?
15019.e: In the first elections with women’s suffrage in 1971, eleven women entered the National Council.
15019.m: In 1971 the first eleven women were elected to the National Council.

15020.q: What does each canton form in the National Council elections?
15020.e: In the National Council elections each canton is one constituency. The parties put up lists in each canton.
15020.m: Each canton is one constituency in National Council elections.

15021.q: How many times a year do the regular sessions of Parliament take place?
15021.e: Parliament meets four times a year for sessions of three weeks each: in spring, summer, autumn and winter.
15021.m: Parliament meets four times a year in sessions.

15022.q: What is another name for the National Council?
15022.e: Because it is much larger than the Council of States, with 200 members, the National Council is also called the Large Chamber.
15022.m: The National Council is also called the Large Chamber.

15023.q: Who does the Council of States represent?
15023.e: The Council of States is the chamber of the cantons. Each canton has almost the same weight, whatever its size.
15023.m: The Council of States represents the cantons.

15024.q: How many members of the Council of States does a canton like Zurich or Uri have?
15024.e: In the Council of States population does not count: big Zurich and little Uri each have two seats.
15024.m: Large and small cantons have the same number of seats in the Council of States.

15025.q: Which cantons have only one seat in the Council of States?
a: The former half-cantons such as Basel-Stadt
The border cantons such as Geneva
The mountain cantons such as the Grisons
The lake cantons such as Zug
15025.e: Basel-Stadt, Basel-Landschaft, Obwalden, Nidwalden, Appenzell Ausserrhoden and Appenzell Innerrhoden each have one seat in the Council of States.
15025.m: The six former half-cantons each have one seat in the Council of States.

15026.q: What is the assembly called when the National Council and the Council of States meet together?
15026.e: Together, the members of the National Council and the Council of States form the United Federal Assembly. It elects the Federal Council, for example.
15026.m: The United Federal Assembly is made up of both chambers.

15027.q: How many members does the United Federal Assembly have?
15027.e: 200 members of the National Council and 46 of the Council of States add up to 246.
15027.m: The United Federal Assembly has 246 members.

15028.q: Who decides how the members of the Council of States are elected?
15028.e: The Federal Constitution leaves the voting procedure to the cantons. Today the people elect the members of the Council of States in all cantons.
15028.m: Each canton decides for itself how it elects its members of the Council of States.

15029.q: Who elects the members of the Council of States in the cantons today?
15029.e: In the past, the cantonal parliaments elected the members of the Council of States in some cantons. Today the people elect them everywhere.
15029.m: Members of the Council of States are elected by the people today.

15030.q: What rights does the Council of States have compared with the National Council?
15030.e: Both chambers have equal rights. A law is only passed if both the National Council and the Council of States agree.
15030.m: The National Council and the Council of States have equal rights.

15031.q: What happens to a new law if the National Council says yes but the Council of States says no?
a: It only applies in large cantons
15031.e: A law needs the approval of both councils. If they still cannot agree after several rounds of debate, the law has failed.
15031.m: A law needs a yes from both the National Council and the Council of States.

15032.q: In which year could women be elected to the Council of States for the first time?
15032.e: In 1971 women in Switzerland got the right to vote and stand for election at federal level. In the same year the first woman was elected to the Council of States.
15032.m: Since 1971 women can be elected to the Council of States.

15033.q: What is another name for the Council of States?
15033.e: With 46 members, the Council of States is much smaller than the National Council and is therefore called the Small Chamber.
15033.m: The Council of States is also called the Small Chamber.

15034.q: Within what time limit must the signatures for an optional referendum be collected?
15034.e: After a law is published, there are 100 days left for the referendum.

15035.q: What is the aim of a popular initiative?
a: To propose a change to the Federal Constitution
To stop a law passed by Parliament afterwards
15035.e: With a popular initiative, citizens can demand an addition to or change in the Federal Constitution. With a referendum, on the other hand, laws are stopped.
15035.m: With a popular initiative the people propose a change to the constitution.

15036.q: What is the “double majority” in votes on the constitution?
a: A majority of the people and a majority of the cantons
A majority in the National Council and in the Federal Council
Two votes on the same day
15036.e: A change to the constitution is only accepted if both the majority of voters (popular majority) and the majority of the cantons (cantonal majority) agree.
15036.m: Changes to the constitution need the popular majority and the cantonal majority.

15037.q: When must there always be a popular vote in Switzerland (mandatory referendum)?
a: For every change to the Federal Constitution
15037.e: Every change to the Federal Constitution must be put to the people and the cantons. That is why this referendum is called mandatory.
15037.m: Changes to the constitution always go to the people.

15038.q: How often do national votes usually take place in Switzerland?
15038.e: Each year the Confederation usually sets four voting Sundays. Several proposals can be voted on on one Sunday.
15038.m: National votes usually take place four times a year.

15040.q: When did Swiss men approve votes for women at federal level?
15040.e: On 7 February 1971 men approved votes for women with around 66 per cent voting yes. A first attempt had failed in 1959.
15040.m: Since 1971 women in Switzerland have been able to vote and be elected at federal level.

15041.q: Which canton had to be forced by the Federal Supreme Court in 1990 to give women the vote?
15041.e: The Landsgemeinde of Appenzell Innerrhoden still rejected votes for women in April 1990. In November 1990 the Federal Supreme Court ruled that this was against the constitution.
15041.m: Appenzell Innerrhoden was the last canton to give women the vote, in 1990.

15042.q: From what age can you vote and stand for election at federal level in Switzerland?
15042.e: Since 1991 the voting age at federal level has been 18; before that it was 20.
15042.m: At federal level you can vote from the age of 18.

15043.q: In which two cantons is there still a Landsgemeinde today?
15043.e: At the Landsgemeinde, voters gather in the open air and vote by raising their hands. Today this only happens in Glarus and Appenzell Innerrhoden.
15043.m: Glarus and Appenzell Innerrhoden still hold a Landsgemeinde.

19175.q: What is the lead of a pencil mainly made of?
19175.e: Despite its name, a pencil contains no lead. The core is a mixture of graphite and clay.
19175.m: Pencil leads contain graphite, not lead.

19176.q: What is the atomic number of carbon?
19176.e: Carbon atoms have 6 protons in their nucleus. The number 12 is the mass number of the most common carbon atom.

19177.q: Which gas is produced when carbon burns completely with enough oxygen?
19177.e: In complete combustion, each carbon atom joins with two oxygen atoms. This produces CO2.
19177.m: Complete combustion of carbon produces carbon dioxide.

19178.q: What is the branch of chemistry that studies carbon compounds called?
19178.e: Organic chemistry studies carbon compounds such as sugars, fats and plastics. People used to believe that only living things could make such substances.
19178.m: Organic chemistry is the chemistry of carbon.

19179.q: Which metal is liquid at room temperature?
19179.e: Mercury melts at about -39 °C. It is poisonous, so it is hardly used in thermometers any more.
19179.m: Mercury is the only metal that is liquid at room temperature.

19180.q: Which property do all metals have in common?
a: They are solid at room temperature
19180.e: Metals contain electrons that can move freely. That is why all metals conduct electricity and heat.

19181.q: Which metals is bronze mainly made of?
19181.e: Bronze is an alloy of copper and tin. It gave the Bronze Age its name.
19181.m: Bronze is an alloy of copper and tin.

19182.q: Which of these metals is attracted by a magnet?
19182.e: Iron, nickel and cobalt are ferromagnetic. Copper, aluminium and gold are not attracted by an ordinary magnet.

19183.q: Which metal is usually used for electric cables in the home because it conducts so well?
19183.e: Copper conducts electricity very well and is easy to shape into wires. Only silver conducts slightly better, but it is much more expensive.
19183.m: Electric cables are usually made of copper.

a: An alloy of iron and carbon
An alloy of copper and zinc
19184.e: Steel is iron with a little carbon and often other additives. This makes it stronger and easy to work with.
19184.m: Steel is an alloy of iron and a little carbon.

19185.q: Which light metal is used for drinks cans and kitchen foil?
19185.e: Aluminium is light, easy to shape and does not rust through. In Switzerland, used aluminium cans can be collected separately and recycled.
19185.m: Aluminium is a light metal that is easy to shape.

19186.q: Which non-metal is liquid at room temperature?
19186.e: Bromine is a red-brown, poisonous liquid. It is the only non-metal that is liquid at room temperature.

19187.q: Which yellow, solid non-metal is often found at volcanoes?
19187.e: Sulphur forms yellow crystals that are deposited from gases at volcanoes. When it burns, it has a sharp smell.

19188.q: Which property do most non-metals have?
19188.e: Most non-metals lack freely moving electrons. That is why they conduct electricity and heat poorly. Graphite is a well-known exception.
19188.m: Most non-metals are poor conductors of electricity.

19189.q: Which gas makes up about 78 % of the air?
19189.e: Nitrogen is the main part of the air. The gas is colourless and reacts only with difficulty with other substances.
19189.m: Most of the air is nitrogen.

19190.q: Which non-metal is often used to disinfect swimming pool water?
19190.e: Chlorine and its compounds kill bacteria in pool water. That is where the typical indoor pool smell comes from.
19190.m: Chlorine keeps pool water free of germs.

19191.q: Which element has been added to table salt in Switzerland since 1922 to prevent goitre?
19191.e: A lack of iodine can lead to an enlarged thyroid gland, called a goitre. That is why in 1922 Switzerland became the first country in the world to introduce iodised table salt.
19191.m: Iodised salt protects against a lack of iodine.

19192.q: How can you recognise a chemical reaction?
a: A substance is only broken into pieces
A substance only changes its state
19192.e: In a chemical reaction, substances with new properties are formed. Energy is often involved too, for example as heat or light.

19193.q: What are the starting substances of a chemical reaction called?
19193.e: The substances before the reaction are called reactants. The newly formed substances are called products.
19193.m: In a reaction, reactants turn into products.

a: A substance that speeds up a reaction and is not used up
A substance that stops every reaction immediately
The end product of a reaction
A substance that burns during the reaction
19194.e: A catalyst lowers the activation energy needed, so a reaction runs faster. At the end it is left unchanged.
19194.m: A catalyst speeds up a reaction without being used up.

19195.q: What do you call a reaction that releases heat?
19195.e: Exothermic reactions give off energy to their surroundings, for example a fire. Endothermic reactions take in energy.

19196.q: In a chemical reaction in a closed container, what happens to the total mass?
19196.e: According to the law of conservation of mass, no atoms are lost and none are added. They are only rearranged.
19196.m: Mass is conserved in chemical reactions.

19197.q: Which process is a chemical reaction?
19197.e: When baking, new substances are formed, for example the brown crust. Melting, grinding and evaporating only change a substance on the outside.
19197.m: Chemical reactions take place when baking.

19198.q: Which three things does a fire need?
19198.e: These three conditions form the fire triangle. If one of them is missing, the fire goes out.
19198.m: A fire needs fuel, oxygen and enough heat.

19199.q: Why can you smother a small fire with a fire blanket?
a: The blanket keeps the oxygen away
The blanket cools the fire a lot
The blanket takes away the fuel
The blanket makes the flames wet
19199.e: The fire blanket separates the fire from the air. Without oxygen, the burning cannot continue.
19199.m: Without oxygen, a fire goes out.

19200.q: Why must you never put out burning oil with water?
a: The water turns to steam suddenly and sprays burning oil
The water makes the oil poisonous
The water gives the fire oxygen
19200.e: Water sinks below the hot oil and turns to steam explosively. It carries burning droplets of oil with it, and a huge flame shoots up.
19200.m: Put out burning oil with a lid and never with water.

19201.q: Which poisonous gas is produced when something burns with too little oxygen?
19201.e: If there is not enough oxygen, burning substances that contain carbon produce carbon monoxide. The gas is colourless, odourless and very poisonous.
19201.m: Carbon monoxide is an invisible and dangerous gas.

19202.q: What do you call an extremely fast burning with a bang and a shock wave?
19202.e: In an explosion, the burning happens in fractions of a second. The hot gases expand suddenly.
19202.m: An explosion is a very fast burning.

19203.q: Why does wood wool burn more easily than a thick block of wood?
a: It has a much larger surface
It is made of a different wood
It is heavier than the block
19203.e: Finely divided materials have a lot of surface where oxygen can attack. That is why they catch fire more quickly.
19203.m: The more finely a fuel is divided, the more easily it burns.

19204.e: Rust forms when iron reacts with oxygen and water. This produces iron oxides that contain water.
19204.m: Rust is an oxide of iron.

19205.q: What does iron need in order to rust?
19205.e: Iron only rusts when oxygen and moisture are present. Salt, for example road salt in winter, speeds up rusting.
19205.m: Iron rusts with air and moisture.

19206.q: What do you call a reaction in which a substance combines with oxygen?
19206.e: Originally, every reaction with oxygen was called oxidation. Today the term generally means the loss of electrons.
19206.m: When a substance combines with oxygen, it is called oxidation.

19207.q: What do you call the reaction in which oxygen is removed from an oxide?
19207.e: In reduction, oxygen is removed from a substance. This is how iron is extracted from iron ore in a blast furnace, for example.
19207.m: Reduction is the opposite of oxidation.

19208.q: Why do copper roofs turn green over time?
a: The colour of the copper fades
The copper melts in the sun
19208.e: Copper reacts with substances in the air and rain. A green layer forms, the patina, which protects the metal underneath.
19208.m: Green patina protects copper from further weathering.

19209.q: Why does a cut apple turn brown in the air?
a: Substances in the apple react with oxygen
The water in the apple evaporates
The sugar in the apple melts
19209.e: Enzymes in the apple help substances in it combine with oxygen from the air. This produces brown substances. Lemon juice slows this down.
19209.m: An apple turns brown because it reacts with oxygen.

19210.q: Which acid is found in stomach juice?
19210.e: The stomach makes dilute hydrochloric acid. It helps with digestion and kills many germs.
19210.m: In the stomach, hydrochloric acid helps with digestion.

19211.q: Which acid gives vinegar its sour taste?
19211.e: Vinegar contains acetic acid, which acetic acid bacteria make from alcohol. Kitchen vinegar usually contains about 5 % acid.

19213.q: Which acid do some ants spray to defend themselves?
19213.e: Formic acid was named after ants (Latin ‘formica’), because it used to be obtained from them. It is also found in stinging nettles.
19213.m: Formic acid is named after ants.

19214.q: Which particles do acids release when dissolved in water?
19214.e: Acids release hydrogen ions in water. The more of them there are in the solution, the more acidic it is.
19214.m: Acids release hydrogen ions in water.

19215.q: Which rule applies when diluting a concentrated acid?
a: First the water, then the acid
First the acid, then the water
Pour both in quickly at the same time
19215.e: If you pour water into concentrated acid, the strong heat can make it boil suddenly and spray acid. That is why you add the acid slowly to the water.
19215.m: When diluting, always add the acid to the water, never the other way round.

a: A solution of a base in water
19216.e: When a base dissolves in water, it forms an alkali solution. Alkalis are the chemical opposite of acids.
19216.m: An alkali solution is a base dissolved in water.

19217.q: Which household product often contains a strong alkali?
19217.e: Many drain cleaners contain sodium hydroxide. The strong alkali dissolves hair and grease and is corrosive, so you need gloves.
19217.m: Drain cleaners are often strongly corrosive alkalis.

19218.q: What colour does red litmus paper turn in an alkali?
19218.e: Litmus turns blue in basic solutions. This lets you tell alkalis apart from acids.

19219.q: What is the alkali called that forms when sodium hydroxide dissolves in water?
19219.e: Sodium hydroxide in water gives caustic soda solution. It is used, for example, to make soap and pretzels.
19219.m: Sodium hydroxide in water gives caustic soda solution.

19220.q: What is formed when an acid and an alkali come together in the right amounts?
19220.e: This reaction is called neutralisation. The acidic and basic particles cancel each other out.

19221.q: Which particles are typical of alkalis?
19221.e: Alkalis contain many hydroxide ions. They consist of one oxygen atom and one hydrogen atom and are negatively charged.
19221.m: Hydroxide ions make a solution basic.

19223.q: What does a pH value below 7 mean?
19223.e: The lower the pH value, the more acidic a solution is. Values above 7 mean basic.
19223.m: A pH value below 7 means acidic.

19224.q: What range does the usual pH scale cover?
19224.e: The common pH scale goes from 0 to 14. The neutral point is in the middle.
19224.m: The pH scale usually goes from 0 to 14.

19225.q: What colour does universal indicator show in a neutral solution (pH 7)?
19225.e: Universal indicator turns red to orange in acidic solutions and purple in strongly basic ones. At pH 7 it shows a green colour.
19225.m: Universal indicator turns green in neutral solutions.

19227.q: What can you use to find the pH value of a solution easily?
19227.e: Universal indicator is a mixture of dyes that shows a different colour depending on the pH value. You read the value off a colour chart.
19227.m: Universal indicator shows the pH value by its colour.

19228.q: How many times more acidic is a solution with pH 3 than a solution with pH 4?
19228.e: The pH scale is logarithmic. One step lower means ten times more acidic particles, so 10 times more acidic.
19228.m: Each pH step means a difference by a factor of ten.

19229.q: What is the easiest method to separate sand from water?
19229.e: When filtering, the sand stays in the filter paper. The water flows through as the filtrate.
19229.m: Solid particles are separated from liquids by filtering.

19230.q: How do the Swiss Saltworks get salt from brine?
19230.e: Brine is salty water from underground. When it is evaporated, the water turns to vapour and the salt is left behind.

19231.q: What is the easiest way to separate iron filings from sand?
19231.e: Iron is attracted by a magnet, sand is not. This makes it easy to separate the two.
19231.m: Magnetic substances are separated with a magnet.

19232.q: Which property of substances is used in distilling?
19232.e: When distilling, the substance with the lower boiling point evaporates first. The vapour is cooled and collected as a liquid again.
19232.m: Distilling separates liquids by their boiling points.

19233.q: Which method can separate the dyes in a felt-tip pen?
19233.e: In paper chromatography, the dyes travel through the paper with the solvent at different speeds. This separates them visibly.

19234.q: What do you call solid particles settling at the bottom of a liquid?
19234.e: Heavy particles sink because of gravity and settle. Afterwards you can carefully pour off the liquid.
19234.m: In sedimentation, solid particles settle at the bottom.

19235.q: Which separation method takes place when you brew tea?
19235.e: Hot water draws flavours and colours out of the tea leaves. Drawing substances out with a solvent is called extraction.
19235.m: When making tea, substances are extracted.

20812.q: What is the German word ‘Hallo’ in English?
20812.e: In English you say ‘Hello’ when you greet someone.

20813.q: What is the German greeting ‘Guten Morgen’ in English?
20813.e: ‘Morgen’ means morning, so in the morning you say ‘Good morning’.
20813.m: In the morning you say ‘Guten Morgen’, or ‘Good morning’.

20814.q: What is the German ‘Gute Nacht’ in English?
20814.e: Before going to sleep, you say ‘Good night’ in English and ‘Gute Nacht’ in German.
20814.m: Before sleeping you wish someone ‘Good night’.

20815.q: What is the German ‘Auf Wiedersehen’ in English?
20815.e: When you leave, you say ‘Goodbye’ or just ‘Bye’ in English.

20816.q: What is the German word ‘Danke’ in English?
20816.e: When you thank someone, you say ‘Thank you’ or just ‘Thanks’ in English.

20817.q: What is the German word ‘Bitte’ in English when you ask for something?
20817.e: When you politely ask for something, you say ‘please’ in English.
20817.m: Polite children say ‘bitte’ in German and ‘please’ in English.

20819.q: What is the German sentence ‘Ich heisse Anna’ in English?
20819.e: When you introduce yourself in English, you say ‘My name is ...’.
20819.m: With ‘My name is’ you tell someone your name in English.

20820.q: What is the German number ‘eins’ in English?
20820.e: The number 1 is ‘eins’ in German and ‘one’ in English.

20821.q: What is the German number ‘drei’ in English?
20821.e: The number 3 is ‘drei’ in German and ‘three’ in English. A ‘tree’ is something quite different.

20822.q: What is the German number ‘fünf’ in English?
20822.e: The number 5 is ‘fünf’ in German and ‘five’ in English.

20823.e: ‘Seven’ is the English word for the number 7. It sounds similar to the German ‘sieben’.

20824.q: What is the German number ‘zehn’ in English?
20824.e: The number 10 is ‘zehn’ in German and ‘ten’ in English.

20825.e: ‘Eight’ is the English word for the number 8. In German it is ‘acht’.

20826.q: What is the German number ‘zwölf’ in English?
20826.e: The number 12 is ‘twelve’ in English. It sounds a little like the German ‘zwölf’.

20827.e: ‘Twenty’ is the English word for the number 20. In German it is ‘zwanzig’.

20828.q: What is ‘two plus two’ in English words?
20828.e: Two plus two makes four, and in English you write it as ‘four’.

20829.q: What is the German colour ‘rot’ in English?
20829.e: The colour ‘rot’ in German is ‘red’ in English.

20830.q: What is the German colour ‘blau’ in English?
20830.e: The colour ‘blau’ in German is ‘blue’ in English.

20831.q: What is the German colour ‘grün’ in English?
20831.e: The colour ‘grün’ in German is ‘green’ in English. Grass is green.

20832.q: What is the German colour ‘gelb’ in English?
20832.e: The colour ‘gelb’ in German is ‘yellow’ in English. People often paint the sun yellow.

20833.e: ‘Black’ is ‘schwarz’ in German. The night is often black.

20834.q: What is the German colour ‘weiss’ in English?
20834.e: The colour ‘weiss’ in German is ‘white’ in English. Snow is white.

20835.e: ‘Brown’ is ‘braun’ in German. Chocolate is usually brown.

20836.q: What is the German colour ‘violett’ in English?
20836.e: The colour ‘violett’ in German is usually ‘purple’ in English.

20837.e: ‘Grey’ is ‘grau’ in German. An elephant is grey.

20838.q: What is the German word ‘Hund’ in English?
20838.e: The German word ‘Hund’ means ‘dog’ in English.

20839.q: What is the German word ‘Katze’ in English?
20839.e: The German word ‘Katze’ means ‘cat’ in English.

20841.q: What is the German word ‘Kuh’ in English?
20841.e: The German word ‘Kuh’ means ‘cow’. In Switzerland you see lots of cows in the meadows.

20842.e: ‘Bird’ is ‘Vogel’ in German. Most birds can fly.

20843.q: What is the German word ‘Maus’ in English?
20843.e: The German word ‘Maus’ means ‘mouse’ in English.

20844.e: ‘Fish’ is ‘Fisch’ in German. Fish live in water.

20845.q: What is the German word ‘Schwein’ in English?
20845.e: The German word ‘Schwein’ means ‘pig’ in English.

20846.e: ‘Rabbit’ is ‘Kaninchen’ in German. A hare, on the other hand, is ‘Hase’.

20847.q: What is the German word ‘Mutter’ in English?
20847.e: The German word ‘Mutter’ means ‘mother’; people often say ‘mum’.

20848.q: What is the German word ‘Vater’ in English?
20848.e: The German word ‘Vater’ means ‘father’; people often say ‘dad’.

20849.q: How do you say ‘my sister’ in German?
20849.e: ‘Sister’ is ‘Schwester’ in German. She is a girl with the same parents.

20850.q: What is the German word ‘Bruder’ in English?
20850.e: The German word ‘Bruder’ means ‘brother’ in English.

20851.q: What is the German word ‘Grossmutter’ in English?
20851.e: The German word ‘Grossmutter’ means ‘grandmother’, or ‘granny’ for short.

20852.q: How do you say ‘my grandfather’ in German?
20852.e: A grandfather is the father of your mum or dad. In German he is the ‘Grossvater’.

20853.q: What is the German word ‘Tante’ in English?
20853.e: The German word ‘Tante’ means ‘aunt’. An ‘ant’ is an insect.

20854.q: What is the German word ‘Familie’ in English?
20854.e: The German word ‘Familie’ means ‘family’ in English.

20855.q: What is the German word ‘Kopf’ in English?
20855.e: The German word ‘Kopf’ means ‘head’ in English.

20856.q: What is the German word ‘Bein’ in English?
20856.e: The German word ‘Bein’ means ‘leg’. We walk and run with our legs.

20857.e: ‘Nose’ is ‘Nase’ in German. We smell with it.

20858.q: What is the German word ‘Auge’ in English?
20858.e: The German word ‘Auge’ means ‘eye’. We see with our eyes.

20859.e: ‘Mouth’ is ‘Mund’ in German. We eat and speak with our mouth.

20860.q: What is the German word ‘Fuss’ in English?
20860.e: The German word ‘Fuss’ means ‘foot’. More than one foot are ‘feet’.

20861.e: ‘Ear’ is ‘Ohr’ in German. We hear with our ears.

20862.q: What is the German word ‘Haare’ in English?
20862.e: The German word ‘Haare’ means ‘hair’ in English.

20863.q: What is the German word ‘Apfel’ in English?
20863.e: The German word ‘Apfel’ means ‘apple’ in English.

20864.q: What is the German word ‘Brot’ in English?
20864.e: The German word ‘Brot’ means ‘bread’ in English.

20865.e: ‘Milk’ is ‘Milch’ in German. Swiss cows give a lot of milk.

20866.q: What is the German word ‘Käse’ in English?
20866.e: The German word ‘Käse’ means ‘cheese’. Switzerland is famous for its cheese.

20868.q: What is the German word ‘Ei’ in English?
20868.e: The German word ‘Ei’ means ‘egg’ in English.

20869.e: ‘Banana’ is ‘Banane’ in German. The word looks almost the same in both languages.

20870.q: What is the German word ‘Kuchen’ in English?
20870.e: The German word ‘Kuchen’ means ‘cake’. On birthdays there is often a birthday cake.

20871.q: What is the German word ‘Schuhe’ in English?
20871.e: The German word ‘Schuhe’ means ‘shoes’ in English.

20873.q: What is the German word ‘Socken’ in English?
20873.e: The German word ‘Socken’ means ‘socks’ in English.

20875.q: What is the German word ‘Kleid’ in English?
20875.e: The German word ‘Kleid’ means ‘dress’ in English.

20876.e: ‘Trousers’ is ‘Hose’ in German. In America people also say ‘pants’.

20877.q: What is the German word ‘Rock’ in English?
20877.e: The German word ‘Rock’ means ‘skirt’. A dress is ‘Kleid’ and a shirt is ‘Hemd’.

20878.e: ‘Gloves’ is ‘Handschuhe’ in German, literally ‘hand shoes’. In winter they keep your hands warm.

20879.q: What is the German word ‘Schule’ in English?
20879.e: The German word ‘Schule’ means ‘school’ in English.

20880.q: What is the German word ‘Buch’ in English?
20880.e: The German word ‘Buch’ means ‘book’ in English.

20882.q: What is the German word ‘Lehrerin’ in English?
20882.e: In German a female teacher is ‘Lehrerin’ and a male teacher ‘Lehrer’. In English both are ‘teacher’.

20883.q: Which German word means a ‘rubber’ at school?
20883.e: In Britain an eraser is called a ‘rubber’; in America it is an ‘eraser’. In German it is ‘Radiergummi’.

20884.q: What is the German word ‘Schultasche’ in English?
20884.e: The German word ‘Schultasche’ means ‘schoolbag’ in English.

20885.e: ‘Ruler’ is ‘Lineal’ in German. You use it to draw straight lines.

20886.q: What is the German word ‘Tisch’ in English?
20886.e: The German word ‘Tisch’ means ‘table’ in English.

20887.q: What is the German day ‘Montag’ in English?
20887.e: ‘Montag’ is ‘Monday’. In English the days of the week always start with a capital letter.

20888.e: ‘Friday’ is ‘Freitag’ in German. The two words sound similar.

20889.q: What is the German day ‘Sonntag’ in English?
20889.e: ‘Sonntag’ is ‘Sunday’. In both languages the word contains the sun: ‘Sonne’ and ‘sun’.

20891.q: What is the German day ‘Samstag’ in English?
20891.e: The German day ‘Samstag’ is ‘Saturday’ in English.

20892.e: ‘Tuesday’ is ‘Dienstag’ in German. It comes after Monday.

20893.q: What is the German day ‘Donnerstag’ in English?
20893.e: The German day ‘Donnerstag’ is ‘Thursday’ in English.

20894.q: What is the German word ‘Wochenende’ in English?
20894.e: Saturday and Sunday together make the weekend, in German ‘Wochenende’.

20895.q: What is the German month ‘Januar’ in English?
20895.e: ‘Januar’ is ‘January’. In English, months start with a capital letter.

20896.e: ‘May’ is ‘Mai’ in German. It is the fifth month of the year.

20897.q: What is the German month ‘Dezember’ in English?
20897.e: ‘Dezember’ is ‘December’. Many people celebrate Christmas in December.

20898.e: ‘March’ is ‘März’ in German. It is the third month of the year.

20899.q: What is the German month ‘Juni’ in English?
20899.e: ‘Juni’ is ‘June’. It is the sixth month of the year.

20900.e: ‘July’ is ‘Juli’ in German. It is the seventh month of the year.

20901.q: What is the German month ‘Oktober’ in English?
20901.e: ‘Oktober’ is ‘October’ in English, with a c instead of a k.

20902.q: What is the German word ‘Monat’ in English?
20902.e: The German word ‘Monat’ means ‘month’. The moon is ‘Mond’ in German.

20903.q: How do you say ‘Hello’ (good day) in French?
20903.e: To greet someone in French you say ‘Bonjour’. You hear it everywhere in French-speaking Switzerland.
20903.m: In French you greet someone with ‘Bonjour’.

20904.q: How do you say ‘Thank you’ in French?
20904.e: When you thank someone in French, you say ‘merci’. People in German-speaking Switzerland often say ‘merci’ too.
20904.m: In French you say thank you with ‘merci’.

20905.q: How do you say ‘yes’ in French?
20905.e: ‘Yes’ in French is ‘oui’. You pronounce it roughly like ‘wee’.
20905.m: The French word for yes is ‘oui’.

20906.q: How do you say ‘Goodbye’ in French?
20906.e: When you leave, you say ‘Au revoir’ in French.
20906.m: In French you say goodbye with ‘Au revoir’.

20907.e: The cat is ‘le chat’ in French.
20907.m: The cat is ‘le chat’ in French.

20908.q: How do you say ‘one, two, three’ in French?
20908.e: In French you count ‘un, deux, trois’. ‘Uno, dos, tres’ is Spanish and ‘uno, due, tre’ is Italian.
20908.m: In French you count ‘un, deux, trois’.

20909.e: ‘Rouge’ is the French word for red.
20909.m: The French ‘rouge’ is the colour red.

20910.e: Mother in French is ‘la mère’, with an accent on the first e (è). ‘La mer’ without an accent is the sea.
20910.m: The mother is ‘la mère’ in French.

20911.e: Bread is ‘le pain’ in French. At the bakery you might order ‘un pain’.

20912.q: What is the Swiss word ‘Velo’ in English?
20912.e: In Switzerland a bike is called a ‘Velo’. In English it is a ‘bicycle’ or ‘bike’; a ‘motorbike’ has an engine.
20912.m: A ‘Velo’ is a ‘bicycle’ or ‘bike’ in English.

20913.e: The kitchen is the room where you cook. In German it is ‘Küche’, and to cook is ‘kochen’.

20914.q: What is the German word ‘Schmetterling’ in English?
20914.e: A ‘Schmetterling’ is a butterfly. A dragonfly is ‘Libelle’ and a ladybird is ‘Marienkäfer’.

20915.e: The order is Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, in German Montag, Dienstag, Mittwoch, Donnerstag. So ‘Wednesday’ is ‘Mittwoch’.

20916.q: Which English word is the opposite of ‘expensive’?
20916.e: ‘Cheap’ means costing little money and is the opposite of ‘expensive’.
20916.m: What is not expensive is cheap.

20917.q: What is the German word ‘Wolke’ in English?
20917.e: A ‘Wolke’ is a cloud. A crowd is a large group of people and a clock tells the time.

20918.e: After August comes September, just as in German.

20919.e: ‘Gross’ plus ‘Mutter’ makes ‘Grossmutter’, the grandmother. The grandfather is ‘Grossvater’.

20920.q: What is the Swiss word ‘Rüebli’ in English?
20920.e: In Switzerland a carrot is called a ‘Rüebli’. A cucumber and a cabbage are different vegetables.

20921.q: What does the French word ‘la gare’ mean?
20921.e: ‘La gare’ is the railway station, for example ‘la gare de Lausanne’.
20921.m: Trains leave from the station, the ‘gare’.

20922.q: What word do people in French-speaking Switzerland use for the number 90?
20922.e: In French-speaking Switzerland people say ‘nonante’ for 90. In France they say ‘quatre-vingt-dix’.
20922.m: In French-speaking Switzerland 70 is ‘septante’ and 90 is ‘nonante’.

20923.q: How do you say ‘Friday’ in French?
20923.e: The week goes lundi, mardi, mercredi, jeudi, vendredi, samedi, dimanche. Friday is ‘vendredi’.

20924.q: What does the French word ‘la fenêtre’ mean?
20924.e: ‘La fenêtre’ is the window. The door is ‘la porte’.

20925.q: How do you say ‘red’ in French?
20925.e: Red is ‘rouge’. ‘Jaune’ is yellow, ‘vert’ green and ‘bleu’ blue.
20925.m: The colour red is ‘rouge’ in French.

20926.q: What does the French word ‘le frère’ mean?
20926.e: ‘Le frère’ is the brother and ‘la sœur’ the sister.
20926.m: My brother is ‘mon frère’ in French.

20928.q: What does ‘la pomme de terre’ mean?
20928.e: Literally it means ‘apple of the earth’, and it is the potato. The apple on its own is ‘la pomme’.
20928.m: A potato is ‘la pomme de terre’ in French.

20929.q: Which English sentence has the correct word order?
20929.e: English usually follows subject, verb, object. Time phrases like ‘every day’ go at the end or the start of the sentence.
20929.m: In an English sentence the subject is followed by the verb and then the object.

20930.e: In French, colour adjectives come after the noun, so ‘une voiture rouge’.
20930.m: In French the colour comes after the noun.

20931.q: Which word is missing in the sentence ‘She ___ a sister.’?
20931.e: With he, she and it, the present tense form of ‘to have’ is ‘has’.

20932.q: Which verb form fits the sentence ‘Nous ___ à Berne.’?
20932.e: ‘Nous’ goes with the ending -ons, so ‘nous habitons’.
20932.m: Verbs with ‘nous’ usually end in -ons in the present tense.

a: There are three cats in the garden.
There is three cats in the garden.
It are three cats in the garden.
There be three cats in the garden.
20933.e: For several things you say ‘there are’, for one thing ‘there is’.
20933.m: For the plural you use ‘there are’.

20934.q: What does the sentence ‘Il fait beau aujourd'hui.’ mean?
20934.e: ‘Il fait beau’ describes nice weather, and ‘aujourd'hui’ means today.
20934.m: When the weather is nice, you say ‘il fait beau’ in French.

20935.q: Which indefinite article goes before ‘orange’ in English?
20935.e: Before words that start with a vowel sound you use ‘an’. ‘The’ is the definite article.

20936.q: Which article goes with the French word ‘maison’ (house)?
20936.e: ‘Maison’ is feminine and starts with a consonant, so it is ‘la maison’.
20936.m: The house is feminine in French: ‘la maison’.

20937.q: Which English question word asks about a place?
20937.e: ‘Where’ asks about a place. ‘When’ asks about time, ‘why’ about a reason and ‘who’ about a person.
20937.m: With ‘where’ you ask about a place.

20938.q: How do you ask ‘What's your name?’ in French?
20938.e: ‘S'appeler’ means to be called. With ‘Comment tu t'appelles ?’ you ask someone's name.
20938.m: You ask someone's name with ‘Comment tu t'appelles ?’.

20939.q: Which English question is formed correctly?
20939.e: In the present tense, questions are formed with ‘do’ or ‘does’. With ‘you’ it is ‘do’.
20939.m: English questions in the present tense are formed with ‘do’ or ‘does’.

20940.q: Which word is missing in the question ‘___ she play tennis?’?
20940.e: With he, she and it, a present tense question needs ‘does’. The main verb then stays in its base form.

20941.q: What does the French question word ‘pourquoi’ mean?
20941.e: ‘Pourquoi’ means why. The answer often starts with ‘parce que’ (because).
20941.m: The answer to ‘pourquoi’ often starts with ‘parce que’.

20942.q: How do you ask someone's age in French?
20942.e: In French you ‘have’ an age, so you ask ‘Quel âge as-tu ?’. The answer might be ‘J'ai douze ans’.
20942.m: In French you ask someone's age with ‘Quel âge as-tu ?’.

20943.q: Which word is missing in the question ‘___ much is this T-shirt?’?
20943.e: ‘How much’ asks about a price or an amount you cannot count.
20943.m: In English you ask about the price with ‘How much?’.

20944.q: Which words can start a yes/no question in French?
20944.e: ‘Est-ce que’ turns a statement into a yes/no question, for example ‘Est-ce que tu viens ?’.
20944.m: With ‘est-ce que’ a statement becomes a yes/no question.

20945.q: What is the negative of ‘I like fish.’?
20945.e: In the present tense you make negatives with ‘don't’ or ‘doesn't’. With ‘I’ it is ‘don't’.
20945.m: With ‘I’, ‘you’, ‘we’ and ‘they’ you use ‘don't’ for the negative.

20946.q: Which word is missing in the sentence ‘He ___ speak French.’?
20946.e: With he, she and it you make the present tense negative with ‘doesn't’. The verb stays in its base form.
20946.m: With ‘he’ you use ‘doesn't’ and the base form of the verb.

20947.q: What is the negative of ‘Je mange.’?
20947.e: In French, ‘ne’ and ‘pas’ go around the verb.
20947.m: In a French negative the verb sits between ‘ne’ and ‘pas’.

20948.q: What does ‘Je ne sais pas.’ mean?
20948.e: ‘Savoir’ means to know and ‘je sais’ means I know. With ‘ne ... pas’ it becomes ‘I don't know’.
20948.m: If you don't know something, you say ‘Je ne sais pas’ in French.

20949.q: What does the French negative ‘ne ... jamais’ mean?
20949.e: ‘Jamais’ means never. ‘Rien’ means nothing and ‘personne’ nobody.
20949.m: With ‘ne ... jamais’ you say ‘never’ in French.

20950.q: Which word is missing in the sentence ‘They ___ at home yesterday.’?
20950.e: ‘Yesterday’ needs the past tense of ‘to be’. With ‘they’ it is ‘were’, and the negative is ‘weren't’.
20950.m: With ‘they’ the negative past of ‘to be’ is ‘weren't’.

20951.q: What is the negative of ‘J'ai un chat.’?
a: Je ne pas ai un chat.
20951.e: Before a vowel ‘ne’ becomes ‘n'’. After the negative, ‘un’ usually becomes ‘de’.

20952.q: Which English sentence is a correct negative?
20952.e: With ‘I’ you use ‘don't’. A double negative like ‘haven't got no’ is wrong in standard English.
20952.m: In English you only use one negative per sentence.

20953.e: A sister is a female person, so you replace her with ‘she’.
20953.m: For a female person you use ‘she’ in English.

20954.q: Which English pronoun replaces ‘Tom and I’ as the subject?
20954.e: ‘Tom and I’ together are ‘we’ when they are the subject. ‘Us’ is the object form.
20954.m: I and another person together are ‘we’.

20955.q: Which French pronoun is often used instead of ‘nous’ in everyday speech?
20955.e: In everyday speech people often say ‘on’ for we, for example ‘On va au cinéma ?’. The verb is then in the third person singular.
20955.m: In everyday French many people say ‘on’ instead of ‘nous’.

20956.e: For a group made up only of females you use ‘elles’.
20956.m: In French you replace several girls or women with ‘elles’.

20957.q: What is the polite form of ‘you’ in French?
20957.e: ‘Vous’ is the polite form and also the plural of ‘tu’.
20957.m: In French you address adults you don't know well with ‘vous’.

20958.q: Which word is missing in the question ‘Can you help ___?’ when you mean yourself?
20958.e: After a verb you use the object form. The object form of ‘I’ is ‘me’.
20958.m: After a verb you use ‘me’ instead of ‘I’.

20959.q: Which French pronoun replaces ‘Marc et Julie’?
20959.e: As soon as a group includes a male person, you use ‘ils’.
20959.m: In French a mixed group is replaced with ‘ils’.

20960.q: What do you normally use the English pronoun ‘it’ for?
a: for a thing or an animal
20960.e: ‘It’ stands for things and usually also for animals. For people you use ‘he’ or ‘she’.
20960.m: In English you replace things with ‘it’.

20961.e: ‘To buy’ is ‘kaufen’ in German. ‘Verkaufen’ means to sell and ‘bezahlen’ to pay.

20962.q: What does the French verb ‘aller’ mean?
20962.e: ‘Aller’ means to go. It is irregular, for example ‘je vais’.
20962.m: The verb ‘aller’ means to go and is irregular.

20963.q: What does the French verb ‘faire’ mean?
20963.e: ‘Faire’ means to make or to do, for example ‘faire du sport’.
20963.m: If you do sport, you say ‘je fais du sport’ in French.

20964.e: ‘To forget’ is ‘vergessen’ in German. ‘Verlieren’ means to lose and ‘vermissen’ to miss.

20965.q: What does the French verb ‘prendre’ mean?
20965.e: ‘Prendre’ means to take, for example ‘prendre le train’. To give is ‘donner’.
20965.m: In French you take the train with ‘prendre le train’.

20966.e: ‘To understand’ is ‘verstehen’ in German. In English the past form is ‘understood’.

20967.q: What does the French verb ‘vouloir’ mean?
20967.e: ‘Vouloir’ means to want. The polite form ‘je voudrais’ means ‘I would like’.
20967.m: With ‘je voudrais’ you politely say what you would like in French.

20968.q: What does the French verb ‘venir’ mean?
20968.e: ‘Venir’ means to come, for example ‘Tu viens avec moi ?’ (Are you coming with me?). To stay is ‘rester’ and to wait ‘attendre’.
20968.m: The French verb ‘venir’ means to come.

20969.q: Which verb form fits the sentence ‘He ___ to school every day.’?
20969.e: With he, she and it the verb gets an -s in the simple present; with ‘go’ it is ‘goes’.
20969.m: With ‘he’, ‘she’ and ‘it’ the verb gets an -s in the present tense.

20970.q: Which verb form fits the sentence ‘Je ___ français.’?
20970.e: For verbs ending in -er, the form with ‘je’ ends in -e, so ‘je parle’.
20970.m: For -er verbs the form with ‘je’ ends in -e.

20971.q: Which verb form fits the question ‘Tu ___ un frère ?’?
20971.e: In the present tense ‘avoir’ goes j'ai, tu as, il a. So ‘tu’ needs ‘as’.

20972.q: Which verb form fits the question ‘Vous ___ suisses ?’?
20972.e: With ‘vous’ the verb ‘être’ is ‘êtes’. ‘Sommes’ goes with ‘nous’.

20973.q: Which verb form fits the sentence ‘I ___ hungry.’?
20973.e: With ‘I’ the verb ‘to be’ is always ‘am’.

20974.q: Which verb form fits the sentence ‘Ils ___ au cinéma.’?
20974.e: With ‘ils’ the verb ‘aller’ is ‘vont’. ‘Je vais’, ‘il va’ and ‘vous allez’ are other persons.

20975.q: Which word is missing in the sentence ‘Look! It ___ raining.’?
20975.e: For something happening right now you use the present progressive, with ‘is’ for ‘it’.
20975.m: What is happening right now goes in the present progressive in English.

20976.q: Which verb form fits the sentence ‘Nous ___ nos devoirs.’?

20977.q: What is the simple past of ‘go’?
20977.e: ‘Go’ is irregular; its simple past is ‘went’. ‘Gone’ is the past participle.

20978.q: What is the simple past of ‘buy’?
20978.e: ‘Buy’ is irregular and its simple past is ‘bought’. ‘Brought’ belongs to ‘bring’.

20979.q: Which verb form fits the sentence ‘Yesterday I ___ a film.’?
20979.e: ‘Yesterday’ needs the simple past. With regular verbs you add -ed.
20979.m: Regular verbs form the simple past with -ed.

20980.q: Which auxiliary verb fits the sentence ‘J'___ mangé une pomme.’?
20980.e: Most verbs form the passé composé with ‘avoir’. With ‘je’ it is ‘j'ai’.
20980.m: Most verbs form the passé composé with ‘avoir’.

20981.q: Which auxiliary verb fits the sentence ‘Elle ___ allée à Genève.’?
20981.e: ‘Aller’ forms the passé composé with ‘être’. That is why it is ‘elle est allée’.
20981.m: The verb ‘aller’ forms the passé composé with ‘être’.

20982.q: Which signal word typically shows the simple past in English?
20982.e: ‘Yesterday’ points to a finished action in the past.
20982.m: With ‘yesterday’ or ‘last week’ English usually uses the simple past.

20983.q: Which short answer fits ‘Did you see the match?’?
20983.e: The question starts with ‘did’, so the short answer uses ‘did’.
20983.m: In a short answer you repeat the auxiliary verb of the question.

20984.q: What is the past participle of ‘faire’?
20984.e: ‘Faire’ is irregular; the participle is ‘fait’, as in ‘j'ai fait’.

20985.q: What is the past participle of ‘voir’?
20985.e: ‘Voir’ is irregular; the participle is ‘vu’, for example ‘j'ai vu’.

20986.q: What time is ‘It's half past seven’?
20986.e: ‘Half past seven’ means half an hour after seven, so 7.30. In German you say ‘halb acht’, half an hour before eight.
20986.m: With ‘half past’ you add half an hour to the hour.

20987.q: What time is ‘Il est huit heures et quart’?
20987.e: ‘Et quart’ means and a quarter, so a quarter of an hour after eight.
20987.m: With ‘et quart’ you add a quarter of an hour in French.

20988.e: ‘To’ means before. A quarter to nine is 8.45.
20988.m: With ‘quarter to’ there is still a quarter of an hour until the full hour.

20989.e: ‘Midi’ is midday, so 12 o'clock. Midnight is ‘minuit’.
20989.m: At 12 o'clock in the day it is ‘midi’ in French.

20990.q: What time is ‘Il est trois heures moins le quart’?
20990.e: ‘Moins le quart’ means minus a quarter. Three o'clock minus 15 minutes makes 2.45.
20990.m: With ‘moins le quart’ you take away a quarter of an hour.

20991.q: How do you say 10.20 in English?
20991.e: Up to the half hour you say how many minutes ‘past’ the hour it is. 20 minutes after ten is ‘twenty past ten’.
20991.m: Up to the half hour you use ‘past’ in English.

20992.q: What does the English abbreviation ‘a.m.’ mean with a time?
20992.e: ‘A.m.’ comes from the Latin ‘ante meridiem’ and means before noon. After noon is ‘p.m.’.
20992.m: In English, times in the morning are marked ‘a.m.’.

20993.q: What time is ‘Il est dix heures et demie’?
20993.e: ‘Et demie’ means and a half, so half an hour after ten.
20993.m: With ‘et demie’ you add half an hour in French.

20994.e: ‘Abbiegen’ means to turn and ‘links’ means left. Right is ‘rechts’.

20995.e: ‘Tout droit’ means straight on. ‘Allez’ here is the polite command with ‘vous’.
20995.m: If you go ‘tout droit’, you go straight on.

20996.e: ‘À droite’ means to the right. ‘Droite’ here means the right-hand side.
20996.m: If you go ‘à droite’, you turn right.

20997.e: ‘Next to’ is ‘neben’ in German. ‘Hinter’ means behind and ‘gegenüber’ opposite.

20998.q: What does the French phrase ‘en face de’ mean?
20998.e: ‘En face de’ means opposite. Next to is ‘à côté de’.
20998.m: What is ‘en face de’ something is opposite it.

20999.q: Which is the correct way to ask the way to the station in English?
a: How do I get to the station?
Where do I get the station?
What is the way at station?
20999.e: The correct question is ‘How do I get to the station?’. ‘To get to’ means to reach a place.
20999.m: You ask the way in English with ‘How do I get to ...?’.

21000.q: What does ‘la deuxième rue à gauche’ mean?
a: the second street on the left
the second street on the right
the first street on the left
the second crossroads on the right
21000.e: ‘Deuxième’ means second, ‘rue’ street and ‘à gauche’ on the left.

21001.e: ‘Traffic lights’ are the light signals on the road, in German ‘Ampel’. A crossroads is ‘Kreuzung’.

21002.q: What does ‘Je voudrais un croissant, s'il vous plaît.’ mean?
a: Do you have any croissants left?
21002.e: ‘Je voudrais’ means I would like, and ‘s'il vous plaît’ means please. In Switzerland a croissant is often called a ‘Gipfeli’.
21002.m: At the bakery you order politely with ‘Je voudrais ..., s'il vous plaît’.

21004.q: What does ‘L'addition, s'il vous plaît.’ mean in a restaurant?
21004.e: In a restaurant ‘l'addition’ is the bill. The menu is ‘la carte’.
21004.m: To pay, you ask for ‘l'addition’ in French.

21005.q: What is the polite reply to ‘Thank you!’ in English?
21005.e: ‘You're welcome’ is the polite reply. You use ‘Excuse me’ to get someone's attention.

21006.q: When do you say ‘Enchanté’ in French?
21006.e: ‘Enchanté’ means pleased to meet you and is said when you meet someone for the first time. Women write ‘enchantée’.
21006.m: When you meet someone, you say ‘Enchanté’ in French.

21007.q: What do you say in English when someone sneezes?
21007.e: After a sneeze you say ‘Bless you!’, like ‘Gesundheit!’ in German.
21007.m: When someone sneezes, you say ‘Bless you!’ in English.

21008.e: ‘Bientôt’ means soon. You say it to someone you will see again soon.
21008.m: With ‘À bientôt’ you say ‘see you soon’ in French.

21010.m: To apologise in French, you say ‘Je suis désolé’.

21029.q: What is the plural of the French noun ‘le cheval’?
21029.e: Most nouns ending in ‘-al’ form their plural with ‘-aux’. Exceptions include ‘bals’, ‘festivals’ and ‘carnavals’.
21029.m: Nouns ending in ‘-al’ usually end in ‘-aux’ in the plural.

21095.q: Which side of the road do people drive on in Great Britain?
21095.e: In the United Kingdom and Ireland, traffic drives on the left. In Switzerland and almost all of mainland Europe, people drive on the right.
21095.m: In Great Britain, traffic drives on the left.

22568.q: What colour do you get when you mix red and white?
22568.e: White makes colours lighter. Red turns into a light red, which we call pink.
22568.m: Red with lots of white turns pink.

22569.q: What colour is the sky on a clear day?
22569.e: Sunlight is spread out in the air. Blue light is scattered the most, which is why the sky looks blue.
22569.m: In fine weather the sky is blue.

22570.q: What colour do you get when you mix black and white?
22570.e: Black and white together make grey. With more white, the grey gets lighter.
22570.m: Black and white together make grey.

22571.q: How many colours do people usually count in a rainbow?
22571.e: A rainbow appears when sunlight shines through raindrops. People usually count seven colours, from red to violet.
22571.m: A rainbow usually has seven colours.

22572.q: How many sides does a square have?
22572.e: A square has four sides. All four sides are the same length.
22572.m: A square has four sides of equal length.

22573.q: How many corners does a hexagon have?
22573.e: A hexagon has six corners. The cells of a honeycomb have this shape.

22574.q: What shape is each face of a dice?
22574.e: A dice has six faces. Each face is a square.
22574.m: Each face of a dice is a square.

22575.q: What do you call a shape that is completely round, like a ball?
22575.e: A sphere is round on all sides. A ball or a marble has this shape.
22575.m: A ball has the shape of a sphere.

22576.q: What shape is a stop sign?
22576.e: The stop sign is a red octagon with eight corners. That way you can recognise it even from behind.
22576.m: The stop sign is a red octagon.

22580.q: How many legs do two dogs have altogether?
22580.e: A dog has 4 legs. Two dogs have 4 + 4 = 8 legs.
22580.m: Two dogs have eight legs altogether.

22582.q: What is a baby cow called?
22582.e: A baby cow is called a calf. A foal is a young horse.
22582.m: A cow's baby is called a calf.

22583.q: How many legs does a beetle have?
22583.e: Beetles are insects. All insects have six legs.
22583.m: Insects such as beetles have six legs.

22584.q: Which animal in the Alps hibernates for a long time in winter?
22584.e: The marmot sleeps for many months in winter in its burrow underground. The ibex and the chamois stay awake in winter.
22584.m: The marmot sleeps through the winter in its burrow.

22585.q: What do fish use to breathe underwater?
22585.e: Fish take oxygen out of the water with their gills. They use their fins for swimming.

22586.q: Which of these animals lays eggs?
22586.e: Hens are birds and lay eggs. Cows, horses and sheep give birth to live young.

22587.q: Besides water, what does a plant need to grow?
22587.e: Plants need sunlight. With light, water and air they make their own food.
22587.m: Plants need light and water to grow.

22588.q: Which part of a plant is usually in the soil?
22588.e: The root holds the plant firmly in the ground. It also takes up water from the soil.
22588.m: The root holds the plant in the soil.

22589.q: Which tree do acorns grow on?
22589.e: Acorns are the fruit of the oak tree. Squirrels and wild boar love to eat them.
22589.m: Acorns grow on the oak tree.

22590.q: Which flower is a well-known symbol of the Alps?
22590.e: Edelweiss grows high up in the mountains. It has white, felt-like flowers and is protected in Switzerland.
22590.m: Edelweiss is the famous flower of the Alps.

22591.q: Which tree stays green in winter too?
22591.e: The fir tree has needles that it keeps in winter. Beech, oak and maple lose their leaves in autumn.
22591.m: The fir tree stays green even in winter.

22592.q: Which plant has lots of spines and often grows in the desert?
22592.e: The cactus stores water in its thick stem. Its spines protect it from animals.
22592.m: The cactus stores water and has spines.

22593.q: Which country is the city of Paris in?
22593.e: Paris is the capital of France. France is one of Switzerland's neighbours.
22593.m: Paris is the capital of France.

22594.q: In which city do the Swiss Federal Council and Parliament work?
22594.e: Bern is the federal city of Switzerland. The Federal Palace is there.
22594.m: The Swiss government works in Bern.

22595.q: Which country is a neighbour of Switzerland?
22595.e: Switzerland has five neighbouring countries: Germany, France, Italy, Austria and Liechtenstein.
22595.m: Austria is a neighbour of Switzerland.

22596.q: In which country do kangaroos live in the wild?
22596.e: In the wild, kangaroos are found only in Australia and on a few nearby islands.
22596.m: Kangaroos live in the wild in Australia.

22597.q: Which language do people speak in Italy?
22597.e: People in Italy speak Italian. Italian is also spoken in Ticino, a Swiss canton.

22598.q: Which country is the city of Tokyo in?
22598.e: Tokyo is the capital of Japan. Japan is made up of many islands.
22598.m: Tokyo is the capital of Japan.

22599.q: What shape is the Swiss national flag?
22599.e: The Swiss national flag is square. Only very few countries have a flag like this, for example the Vatican.

22600.q: What can you see in the middle of the Swiss flag?
22600.e: In the middle of the red Swiss flag there is a white cross. It is the symbol of Switzerland.
22600.m: The Swiss flag shows a white cross.

22601.q: Which country has a flag with a red circle on a white background?
22601.e: The red circle on Japan's flag stands for the sun. Japan is also called the Land of the Rising Sun.
22601.m: Japan's flag shows a red sun.

22602.q: What colours is the flag of Italy?
22602.e: The flag of Italy has three vertical stripes in green, white and red.
22602.m: The Italian flag is green, white and red.

22603.q: Which country has a black, red and gold flag?
22603.e: The flag of Germany has three horizontal stripes in black, red and gold. The flag of Austria is red, white and red.
22603.m: The German flag is black, red and gold.

22604.q: Which flag shows a circle of twelve yellow stars on blue?
22604.e: The flag of Europe is blue with twelve yellow stars in a circle. The number twelve stands for completeness.
22604.m: The flag of Europe has twelve yellow stars in a circle.

22605.q: Who bakes fresh bread every morning?
22605.e: The baker bakes bread, croissants and plaited Swiss loaves. Bakers often start work in the middle of the night.

22606.q: Who brings letters and parcels to our homes?
22606.e: The postman works for the post office. He puts letters and parcels in the letterboxes.
22606.m: The postman brings letters and parcels.

22607.q: How many wheels does a bike have?
22607.e: A bike has two wheels, one at the front and one at the back. A tricycle has three.

22608.e: A train runs on rails. In Switzerland, lots of people travel by train.

22609.q: Which vehicle flies with a big propeller on its roof?
22609.e: A helicopter has a big spinning rotor on top. With it, it can take off straight up and hover in the air.
